# Clustarr Phase B — Library Layer Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Deliver the eleven pure-Go library packages every later milestone builds on — release parsing, the TRaSH quality model, naming, ffprobe, transcode planning, Torznab/Newznab, the Cardigann engine, subtitles, metadata clients, import-list clients, and filesystem/rate-limit primitives — each with real fixtures, no Kubernetes types and no network in tests.

**Architecture:** Each package is a leaf under `pkg/` owned by exactly one task and one implementer; the only cross-package imports allowed inside Phase B are the ones listed in each task's **Interfaces → Consumes** block, and every one of those was reconciled by the controller against the producing task's **Produces** block before dispatch. Dependencies are added once, serially, by the controller (Task B0) and kept alive through `hack/deps/deps.go`; workers never touch `go.mod`. The eleven package tasks (B1–B11) run in parallel on disjoint paths; B0 runs before them and B12 (tidy and phase gate) after.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27; `github.com/moistari/rls`, `github.com/dlclark/regexp2`, `gopkg.in/vansante/go-ffprobe.v2`, `github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery`, `github.com/antchfx/xmlquery`, `github.com/tidwall/gjson`, `github.com/goccy/go-yaml`, `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`, `github.com/Masterminds/sprig/v3`, `github.com/asticode/go-astisub`, `github.com/cyruzin/golang-tmdb`, `go.uploadedlobster.com/musicbrainzws2`, `github.com/lithammer/fuzzysearch`, `github.com/gabriel-vasile/mimetype`, `github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/v2`, `golang.org/x/time`, `golang.org/x/net`; testify; `httptest` for every provider client.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-clustarr-design.md` (§7 shared packages, lines ~632–740; §9 quality, line ~759; §2 naming) with `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-clustarr-design-amendment-1.md` winning where they disagree. The verified API shapes for each package live in `docs/research/{quality,naming,transcode,indexers,subtitles,metadata,download}.md` — `grep -n '^#'` first, then read the section. Phase context: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-remaining-work.md` Part 2, "Phase B".

## Global Constraints

Copied verbatim from the spec, `CLAUDE.md` and the remaining-work plan. Every task's requirements implicitly include this section.

- Module `github.com/mediactl/clustarr`. Go 1.27. Licence **GPL-3.0**; every Go file starts with the header in `hack/boilerplate.go.txt`.
- **Phase B packages are pure Go.** No task in this plan may import `sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/...`, `github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/k8s`, or any of the five CRD groups `github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/{catalog,index,download,transcode,subtitle}/...`. The one Kubernetes-adjacent import allowed everywhere is `github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1` (aliased `commonv1`), the shared vocabulary of `MediaKind`, `Quality`, `Source`, `Modifier`, `Revision`, `HdrFormat` and `MediaInfo` — reuse those rather than defining parallel enums. One named exception: `pkg/quality` may import `api/catalog/v1alpha1` for `QualityProfileSpec` and its sub-types only (the built-in profiles are shipped as that exact type), never a client. Everything else that later becomes a CRD field is plain Go here; the controllers in Phase C onward convert. Where spec §7 shows a package taking a CRD spec type directly (`transcode.ProfileHash(transcodev1alpha1.TranscodeProfileSpec)`, `subtitles.Plan(subtitlev1alpha1.SubtitleProfileSpec, …)`), the Phase B package takes a local mirror struct with the same field names and scaled-int types as the real generated CRD type, and the Phase E/F controller converts.
- **No `float32`/`float64` in any exported type that will be copied into `api/` or exported as a metric.** `resource.Quantity` is a Kubernetes type and therefore unavailable here; use scaled integers (`Milli` thousandths, `Centis` hundredths, `Percent` whole 0–100) for anything that will land in a CRD status. A `float64` is acceptable only for an in-process, never-persisted value such as a fuzzy-match confidence, and the task text must say so where it uses one.
- **Use `github.com/dlclark/regexp2`, not stdlib `regexp`, for TRaSH custom-format patterns** (Go RE2 rejects 157 of the 2791). Set `regexp2.IgnoreCase` and a `MatchTimeout`.
- **Quality profiles are TRaSH-only and opinionated.** Built-in profiles ship as embedded data; custom-format editing is not exposed.
- Logging is `slog` through `context` (`pkg/obs/logging.FromContext`). No package-level logger, no logger struct fields. Outbound provider calls are wrapped in a span via `pkg/obs/tracing.Start`; that is the only `pkg/obs` coupling a Phase B package may have.
- Prometheus metrics use the `clustarr_` prefix and base units. **Never label by title, path or release name.** Phase B packages do not register collectors; they expose counters/durations through return values or callbacks and the services in later phases record them.
- Tests are table-driven with testify; fixtures under the repo-root `testdata/<package>/` directory each task owns (Go tests run with the package directory as CWD, so reference them as `../../testdata/<package>/…`). **No network access in tests**; every HTTP client is exercised against `httptest.Server`. Any test that shells out (`ffprobe`, `ffmpeg`) must `t.Skip` when the binary is absent and must also have a fixture-driven path that runs without it.
- Every exported function that can block takes a `context.Context` first and honours cancellation.
- Malformed input never panics: every parser/decoder has at least one test feeding it garbage, truncated and empty input.

### Rules for parallel agents

These are not style preferences. Violating them corrupts shared state and has already cost this project a full rebuild.

1. **Never run `go get` or `go mod tidy` from a worker agent.** Every dependency this plan needs is added serially by Task B0 before any package task starts. If an implementer finds a module missing from `go.mod`, it reports `NEEDS_CONTEXT` naming the module; it does not add it.
2. **Each task owns disjoint paths.** Path ownership is listed per task. `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `hack/deps/` and `docs/` belong to the controller. Writing outside your owned paths is a review failure.
3. **Commit path-scoped.** Several implementers commit to the same branch concurrently, so every commit is `git -c user.name=appkins -c user.email=nbatkins@gmail.com commit -m "<msg>" -- <your owned paths>`; never `git add -A`, never `git commit -a`. If `.git/index.lock` exists, wait five seconds and retry; do not delete it.
4. **Never `go build` without `-o`.** A bare `go build` drops a `clustarr` binary in the repo root. Verify a package with `go build ./pkg/<x>/...`, `go vet ./pkg/<x>/...`, `go test -count=1 -race ./pkg/<x>/...` and `golangci-lint-v2 run ./pkg/<x>/...`.
5. **Verify, do not trust.** The controller re-runs every gate itself after workers report.

## Execution order: two waves

Four packages consume a sibling Phase B package. Rather than have each define a local copy of the sibling's types and reconcile later, they run in a second wave against the real code:

| Wave | Tasks (parallel within the wave) | Starts when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | B0 | first |
| 1 | B1 release, B3 naming, B4 mediainfo, B6 torznab+newznab, B9 metadata, B10 importlist, B11 fsops+ratelimit | B0 committed |
| 2 | B2 quality (imports `pkg/release`), B5 transcode (imports `pkg/mediainfo`), B7 cardigann (imports `pkg/torznab`, `pkg/newznab`), B8 subtitles (imports `pkg/release`) | every wave-1 task has passed task review |
| 3 | B12 | every wave-2 task has passed task review |

Where a wave-2 task's text shows a local placeholder copy of a sibling's type ("reconciled by controller"), the implementer imports the real package instead, deletes the placeholder, and uses the real names — the controller's dispatch carries the mapping from placeholder names to real ones. A field the real package lacks is `NEEDS_CONTEXT`, not a local re-definition.

Cross-package imports permitted inside Phase B (everything else is forbidden and is a review failure):

| Importer | Imports | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg/quality` | `pkg/release` | custom-format matching runs over `release.ParsedRelease` |
| `pkg/cardigann` | `pkg/torznab`, `pkg/newznab` | definitions emit `torznab.Release`; categories map through `newznab.CategoryID` |
| `pkg/subtitles` | `pkg/release` | `subtitles.Query.Release *release.ParsedRelease` (spec §7) |
| `pkg/transcode` | `pkg/mediainfo` | `Plan` reads a probe |
| `pkg/quality` | `api/catalog/v1alpha1` (types only) | `QualityProfileSpec` is the profile model; built-ins ship as it |
| any | `pkg/obs/logging`, `pkg/obs/tracing`, `pkg/ratelimit` | logging, spans, backoff |

(The controller reconciles this table against every task's Interfaces block before dispatch; if a task needs an import not listed here, it reports `NEEDS_CONTEXT` rather than adding it.)

From `pkg/obs`: **none.** `logging.FromContext(ctx)` and `tracing.Start(ctx, ...)` both key off `context.Context`, and every exported function in this package's `Produces` block below is a pure, synchronous, in-memory string transform with no I/O — `Parse`/`ParseKind`/`ParsePath` do not take a `context.Context` (matching the spec's `func Parse(title string, o Options) (*ParsedRelease, error)` exactly; adding one would invent a shape the spec doesn't have). `regexp2.Regexp.MatchTimeout` (Step 2) is this package's own safety net against catastrophic backtracking — a timeout surfaces as a returned `error`, not a log line, and the caller (`indexarr`'s search worker, which does hold a `ctx`) decides whether to log or trace it. This is a deliberate exception to the general Phase B logging guidance, not an oversight: there is nothing to log until a caller with a context exists.

No other Phase B package is imported (`pkg/release` has no dependency on `pkg/quality`, `pkg/naming`, `pkg/decision`, etc. — those consume `pkg/release`, not the reverse), so no `(reconciled by controller)` placeholder types are needed.

**Interfaces — Produces:**

```go
package release // import "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/release"

// Options configures Parse and ParsePath.
type Options struct {
	// Kind pins the media kind, skipping ClassifyKind. The zero value ("")
	// means auto-detect via ClassifyKind.
	Kind common.MediaKind
	// SeriesType selects the Sonarr-style episode-regex family for TV
	// titles: "standard" (default when empty), "daily" or "anime". Ignored
	// for every other Kind.
	SeriesType string
}

// Hints carries custom-format-only tag detail moistari/rls extracts from a
// title: codec, HDR flags, audio codec/layout, streaming service and
// container. None of these are quality identity (pkg/quality/catalogue
// conditions consume them, not pkg/decision's quality ranking).
type Hints struct {
	Codec     []string // x264, x265, h264, h265, AV1, XviD, VC1, MPEG2
	HDR       []string // HDR10, HDR10+, DV, HLG, PQ, SDR
	Audio     []string // DTS-X, DTS-HD MA, TrueHD, Atmos, EAC3, AC3, AAC, FLAC, Opus, MP3
	Channels  string   // "7.1", "5.1", "2.0"; "" when not present
	Streaming []string // AMZN, NF, DSNP, ATVP, HULU, HMAX, ...
	Container string   // mkv, mp4, avi; "" when not present
}

// MusicInfo is populated when ParsedRelease.ReleaseType == common.ReleaseTypeAlbum.
type MusicInfo struct {
	Artist      string
	Album       string
	Year        int
	Codec       string // MP3, FLAC, AAC, Vorbis, ALAC, WavPack, WAV
	BitrateKbps int32  // 0 when lossless or unknown
	VBR         bool
	SampleBits  int32 // 16 or 24; 0 when unknown/lossy
}

// BookInfo is populated for common.MediaKindBook and common.MediaKindAudiobook.
// Audiobook vs. ebook is a Format value, mirroring Readarr's Edition.IsEbook
// being a property rather than a separate type (docs/research/naming.md §12).
type BookInfo struct {
	Author     string
	Title      string
	Year       int
	Format     string // PDF, MOBI, EPUB, AZW3 (ebook); M4B, MP3, FLAC (audiobook)
	Narrator   string // audiobook only; "" otherwise
	ASIN       string // audiobook only; "" otherwise
	Unabridged bool
}

// ComicInfo is populated for common.MediaKindComic and common.MediaKindIssue.
type ComicInfo struct {
	Series string
	Issue  string // "001", "12.5" (manga chapter), "Annual 1"
	Volume int    // 0 when not a volume-numbered manga release
	Year   int
	Format string // CBZ, CBR, PDF
	Manga  bool
}

// TitleCandidate is one inventory item MatchTitle scores a ParsedRelease against.
type TitleCandidate struct {
	Title string
	Year  int
}

// ParsedRelease is the result of parsing a release title. Field set is
// verbatim from spec §7's pkg/release block.
type ParsedRelease struct {
	Title       string
	Titles      []string
	Year        int
	Quality     common.Quality
	Revision    common.Revision
	Languages   []string
	Group       string
	Hash        string // scene obfuscation hash token, e.g. trailing -a1b2c3d4; "" normally
	Edition     string
	Seasons     []int
	Episodes    []int
	Absolute    []int
	AirDate     *time.Time
	FullSeason  bool
	Partial     bool
	MultiSeason bool
	Special     bool
	ReleaseType common.ReleaseType
	Music       *MusicInfo
	Book        *BookInfo
	Comic       *ComicInfo
	Hints       Hints
	IDs         map[string]string
}

func Parse(title string, o Options) (*ParsedRelease, error)
func ParseKind(title string, kind common.MediaKind) (*ParsedRelease, error) // sugar: Parse(title, Options{Kind: kind})
func ParsePath(path string, o Options) (*ParsedRelease, error)             // strips extension/directory, delegates to Parse
func ClassifyKind(title string) common.MediaKind

// MatchTitle scores p against cands with fuzzysearch.RankMatch on
// CleanTitle(p.Title) vs. CleanTitle(cand.Title), penalized by |year delta|;
// best is the index of the top-scoring candidate, or -1 when cands is empty.
// score follows fuzzysearch's own float-scored ranking (not a status or
// telemetry field — no scaled-int substitute applies here).
func MatchTitle(p *ParsedRelease, cands []TitleCandidate) (best int, score float64)

// Normalize returns title with accents stripped, curly quotes/dashes folded
// and whitespace collapsed, case preserved. It is for display / re-embedding
// (e.g. History), not for equality comparison — use CleanTitle for that.
func Normalize(title string) string

// CleanTitle returns a lower-cased, article-stripped, punctuation-stripped
// form of title, stable across "The Matrix", "THE MATRIX", "Matrix, The" and
// "The  Matrix!" alike. It is the key pkg/decision and the metadata gateway
// match parsed titles against inventory titles with.
func CleanTitle(title string) string

// ApplyTo copies the fields this package parses onto ri, leaving every
// indexer-sourced field (GUID, DownloadURL, Seeders, ...) untouched.
func (p *ParsedRelease) ApplyTo(ri *common.ReleaseInfo)

// Fingerprint is a deterministic 16-hex-char sha256 prefix of
// CleanTitle+Year+Seasons+Episodes+Quality.Name+Group, stable across two
// indexers describing the same content. It is a content-level dedup key,
// distinct from indexarr's own sha1(indexer:guid) Msg-Id (spec §8.7): that
// one dedupes repeat sightings of the *same* indexer/guid pair; this one
// dedupes the *same release* seen through two different indexers, which
// neither guid nor infohash can do when only one of the two carries an
// infohash (a usenet mirror of a scene release, for example).
func (p *ParsedRelease) Fingerprint() string

// Age returns publishedAt's age relative to now at three granularities,
// mirroring Radarr's ReleaseResource.{age,ageHours,ageMinutes} (all
// integers in the source API — see docs/research/naming.md A5 — so no float
// is introduced here). now before publishedAt returns all zeros.
func Age(publishedAt, now time.Time) (days int32, hours int32, minutes int64)

// SizePerMinuteCentiMB returns sizeBytes expressed as hundredths of a
// megabyte per minute of runtime (a scaled int, matching CLAUDE.md's
// Centis convention — pkg/quality.Definition's own MinMBPerMin et al. are
// float64 because that struct lives outside api/ too, but this package
// still avoids float in its own exported surface). runtimeMinutes <= 0
// (unknown runtime) returns -1.
func SizePerMinuteCentiMB(sizeBytes int64, runtimeMinutes int32) int64
```

```go
func TestParseSeriesSingleAndMultiEpisode(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		title    string
		seasons  []int
		episodes []int
	}{
		{"single episode", "Severance.S02E03.Chikhai.Bardo.1080p.ATVP.WEB-DL.DDP5.1.Atmos.H.264-NTb", []int{2}, []int{3}},
		{"dual-token multi", "The.Bear.S03E01E02.720p.HULU.WEB-DL.DDP5.1.H.264-NTb", []int{3}, []int{1, 2}},
```

Run: `go test ./pkg/release/... -run TestParseSeriesAnimeAbsolute -v` — expected `FAIL`: `parseSeries` with `SeriesType: "anime"` currently falls through to the standard patterns, which don't match a leading `[Group]` at all, so `p.Title`/`p.Group` come back empty.

Implement `pkg/release/anime.go`. This is the part `docs/research/quality.md` explicitly says to own rather than trust `rls` for. Order of operations, run **before** the generic `parseGroup` (Step 9) so the anime group wins:
```go
var animeGroupRegex = regexp2.MustCompile(`^\[(?<group>[^\]]+)\][\s_.]*`, regexp2.IgnoreCase)
var animeAbsoluteRegex = regexp2.MustCompile(
	`(?<title>.+?)\s*-\s*(?<abs>\d{2,4})(?:\s*\((?<res>\d{3,4}p)\))?`, regexp2.IgnoreCase)
var animeSeasonEpisodeRegex = regexp2.MustCompile(
	`(?<title>.+?)\s*-\s*S(?<season>\d{1,2})E(?<episode>\d{1,4})`, regexp2.IgnoreCase)

func parseAnime(title string, p *ParsedRelease) error {
	work := title
	if m, _ := animeGroupRegex.FindStringMatch(work); m != nil {
		p.Group = m.GroupByName("group").String()
		work = work[m.Length:]
	}
	if m, _ := animeSeasonEpisodeRegex.FindStringMatch(work); m != nil {
		p.Title = strings.TrimSpace(m.GroupByName("title").String())
		season, _ := strconv.Atoi(m.GroupByName("season").String())
		episode, _ := strconv.Atoi(m.GroupByName("episode").String())
		p.Seasons, p.Episodes = []int{season}, []int{episode}
		return nil
	}
	if m, _ := animeAbsoluteRegex.FindStringMatch(work); m != nil {
		p.Title = strings.TrimSpace(m.GroupByName("title").String())
		abs, _ := strconv.Atoi(m.GroupByName("abs").String())
		p.Absolute = []int{abs}
		return nil
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("release: %q does not match any anime title pattern", title)
}
```
`parseSeries` calls `parseAnime` first when `o.SeriesType == "anime"`, then still calls `parseQualityTags` on the *whole original title* (not `work`) for resolution/source, since those tokens live after the parts `parseAnime` consumed. Do **not** call the generic `parseGroup` (Step 9) when `o.SeriesType == "anime"` and `parseAnime` already set `p.Group` — that is precisely the case `docs/research/quality.md` flags `rls` for getting wrong by using its generic (non-anime-aware) group heuristic, and reusing our own generic `parseGroup` here would reintroduce the same bug via a different regex.

Run: `go test ./pkg/release/... -run TestParseSeriesAnimeAbsolute -v` — expected `PASS`.

```go
		HDR:       r.HDR,
		Audio:     r.Audio,
		Channels:  r.Channels,
		Streaming: r.Other, // rls has no dedicated streaming-service field (quality.md §7.3); Other carries it
		Container: r.Container,
	}
}
```

Implement `pkg/release/normalize.go`:
```go
func Normalize(title string) string {
	return rls.MustClean(title)
}

var trailingArticleRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i),\s*(the|a|an)$`)
var leadingArticleRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^(the|a|an)\s+`)
var nonAlnumRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9 ]+`)
var collapseSpaceRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`\s+`)

func CleanTitle(title string) string {
	s := rls.MustNormalize(title) // lower-cased, accent-stripped, punctuation-collapsed
	s = trailingArticleRegex.ReplaceAllString(s, "")
	s = leadingArticleRegex.ReplaceAllString(s, "")
	s = nonAlnumRegex.ReplaceAllString(s, "")
	s = collapseSpaceRegex.ReplaceAllString(s, " ")
	return strings.TrimSpace(s)
}
```
These four helper regexes are plain `regexp` (stdlib), not `regexp2` — none of them need lookaround, and CLAUDE.md's regexp2 mandate is specifically for TRaSH/`*arr` patterns that do.

Implement `pkg/release/match.go`:
```go
func MatchTitle(p *ParsedRelease, cands []TitleCandidate) (best int, score float64) {
	best = -1
	clean := CleanTitle(p.Title)
	for i, c := range cands {
		s := float64(fuzzy.RankMatchNormalized(clean, CleanTitle(c.Title)))
		if s < 0 { // fuzzysearch returns -1 for no match
			continue
		}
		if c.Year != 0 && p.Year != 0 && c.Year != p.Year {
			s -= 1000 // year mismatch is disqualifying but not a hard reject —
			          // a wrong-year near-exact title still beats no match at all
		}
		if best == -1 || s > score {
			best, score = i, s
		}
	}
	return best, score
}
```
Verify `fuzzy.RankMatchNormalized`'s exact signature and "lower is better vs. higher is better" convention against `go doc github.com/lithammer/fuzzysearch/fuzzy RankMatchNormalized` before writing the real implementation — the sketch above assumes higher-is-better; if the library is the opposite, negate consistently rather than flipping only the year penalty's sign.

Implement `pkg/release/dedup.go`:
```go
func (p *ParsedRelease) Fingerprint() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(CleanTitle(p.Title))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "|%d", p.Year)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "|%v|%v", p.Seasons, p.Episodes)
	b.WriteString("|")
	b.WriteString(p.Quality.Name)
	b.WriteString("|")
	b.WriteString(strings.ToLower(p.Group))
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(b.String()))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:16]
}
```

Implement `pkg/release/age.go`:
```go
func Age(publishedAt, now time.Time) (days int32, hours int32, minutes int64) {
	d := now.Sub(publishedAt)
	if d <= 0 {
		return 0, 0, 0
	}
	minutes = int64(d / time.Minute)
	hours = int32(d / time.Hour)
	days = int32(d / (24 * time.Hour))
	return days, hours, minutes
}

func SizePerMinuteCentiMB(sizeBytes int64, runtimeMinutes int32) int64 {
	if runtimeMinutes <= 0 {
		return -1
	}
	const bytesPerMB = 1024 * 1024
	// (sizeBytes * 100) / (bytesPerMB * runtimeMinutes), reordered to divide last.
	return sizeBytes * 100 / (bytesPerMB * int64(runtimeMinutes))
}
```

**Disagreements found (note vs spec), resolved below:**

1. **Dialect count.** The research note's Part C sketch (`docs/research/naming.md:589`) declares `MediaServerDialect` with `// +kubebuilder:validation:Enum=Plex;Jellyfin;Emby;Kodi` — four values — and its own A3 table documents a full Kodi/NFO row. The real generated type, `api/catalog/v1alpha1/rootfolder_types.go`'s `NamingDialect`, also has four values (`jellyfin;plex;emby;kodi`, default `jellyfin`). **Resolution:** this task implements all four dialects (Jellyfin, Plex, Emby, Kodi), even though the phase-B table's one-line summary only names three ("Jellyfin, Plex and Emby presets") — the generated type is the contract per `CLAUDE.md` ("do not drop fields") and dropping Kodi would make `BuildFolder`/`BuildFile` error on a value the CRD accepts today.
2. **`pkg/naming`'s Go shape.** The note's own sketch (`docs/research/naming.md:602-609`) proposes a `Builder` interface — `Path(ctx context.Context, cfg NamingConfig, target TokenSource, file MediaFile) (dir, filename string, err error)` — taking a `context.Context` and a CRD-shaped `NamingConfig` (kubebuilder tags and all) directly. The spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-clustarr-design.md:723-725`) instead declares a concrete `Engine{Dialect, Colon, MultiEpisode, Overrides}` with `Render(template string, ctx Context) (string, error)` and nine named per-kind methods — no `context.Context` parameter, no interface, no CRD type in sight. **Resolution:** the spec wins (it is dated after the note and is the design of record per `CLAUDE.md`). `pkg/naming` implements the spec's `Engine`/`Render`/nine-method surface verbatim, plus the `BuildFolder`/`BuildFile` generic dispatchers this task's brief additionally requires (not in either source verbatim; justified below in Produces). Neither `context.Context` nor the CRD `NamingConfig` type appears in `pkg/naming`'s API — consistent with Phase B's "no Kubernetes dependency" rule, which the note's own sketch predates.
3. **Nested-brace wrapper syntax.** The note's `AudiobookFolderFormat` example (`docs/research/naming.md:596`) and Radarr's real UI use a doubled-brace form for an optional narrator/ID segment, e.g. `{{Narrator}}` or `{tmdbid-{TmdbId}}`. This task's grammar (Step 1-2 below) is single-pass over non-nesting `\{[^{}]*\}` groups, so nesting is not supported. **Resolution:** stated in Step 12 — the doubled-brace idiom is expressed instead with this grammar's existing space-prefix wrapper, e.g. `{ Narrator}` (see the real, working example the note itself already uses for the same purpose in the Radarr audio tokens: `{[Mediainfo AudioCodec}{ Mediainfo AudioChannels]}` splits one bracket pair across two adjacent single-brace tokens rather than nesting — this task's grammar is built to reproduce exactly that pattern, so it is not a new invention, just consistently applied everywhere the note used nesting instead).

**Interfaces — Produces:**
```go
package naming // github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/naming

// ---- Config, mirrored 1:1 by string value from api/catalog/v1alpha1's
// RootFolder Naming types. pkg/naming cannot import api/catalog (no
// Kubernetes dependency in Phase B); Phase C's catalogarr controller casts
// catalogv1alpha1.NamingDialect(x) -> naming.Dialect(x) etc.

type Dialect string
const (
	DialectJellyfin Dialect = "jellyfin"
	DialectPlex     Dialect = "plex"
	DialectEmby     Dialect = "emby"
	DialectKodi     Dialect = "kodi"
)

type ColonReplacement string
const (
	ColonDelete         ColonReplacement = "delete"
	ColonDash           ColonReplacement = "dash"
	ColonSpaceDash      ColonReplacement = "spaceDash"
	ColonSpaceDashSpace ColonReplacement = "spaceDashSpace"
	ColonSmart          ColonReplacement = "smart"
)

type MultiEpisodeStyle string
const (
	MultiEpisodeExtend        MultiEpisodeStyle = "extend"
	MultiEpisodeDuplicate     MultiEpisodeStyle = "duplicate"
	MultiEpisodeRepeat        MultiEpisodeStyle = "repeat"
	MultiEpisodeScene         MultiEpisodeStyle = "scene"
	MultiEpisodeRange         MultiEpisodeStyle = "range"
	MultiEpisodePrefixedRange MultiEpisodeStyle = "prefixedRange"
)

// Override token keys, verbatim from api/catalog/v1alpha1's NamingToken*
// constants (duplicated by value, not by import).
const (
	TokenMovieFolder     = "movieFolder"
	TokenMovieFile       = "movieFile"
	TokenSeriesFolder    = "seriesFolder"
	TokenSeasonFolder    = "seasonFolder"
	TokenEpisodeFile     = "episodeFile"
	TokenAnimeFile       = "animeFile"
	TokenDailyFile       = "dailyFile"
	TokenArtistFolder    = "artistFolder"
	TokenAlbumFolder     = "albumFolder"
	TokenTrackFile       = "trackFile"
	TokenAuthorFolder    = "authorFolder"
	TokenBookFile        = "bookFile"
	TokenAudiobookFolder = "audiobookFolder"
	TokenAudiobookFile   = "audiobookFile"
	TokenComicFolder     = "comicFolder"
	TokenIssueFile       = "issueFile"
)

type Config struct {
	Dialect           Dialect
	ColonReplacement  ColonReplacement
	MultiEpisodeStyle MultiEpisodeStyle
	Overrides         map[string]string // keys are the Token* constants above

	// Lidarr/Readarr-style global post-processing (note §A2, Lidarr/Readarr
	// NamingConfigResource: replaceSpaces, separator). Zero value = off.
	ReplaceSpaces bool
	Separator     string // e.g. "-", "_", "."
	Case          string // "", "upper", "lower"
}

type Engine struct{ Config Config }

func NewEngine(cfg Config) Engine

// Context is the plain-Go, per-item render input. It is defined here, not
// imported from api/catalog -- every field a token in §A2's tables needs,
// across movie/series/episode/anime/daily/music/book/audiobook/comic.
type Context struct {
	Kind commonv1.MediaKind

	// Movie / Series / Episode identity. ImdbID/TmdbID/TvdbID/TvMazeID are
	// shared across kinds rather than duplicated per-kind (SeriesTvdbID,
	// etc.) because the *arr token names themselves are bare -- {TvdbId},
	// {ImdbId}, {TmdbId}, {TvMazeId} (note §A2, Sonarr token list, line 74)
	// -- with no "Series" prefix, and one Context always describes exactly
	// one item, so there is never a movie id and a series id to
	// disambiguate in the same render call.
	Title, OriginalTitle, Collection, Certification string
	Year                                             int
	ImdbID, TmdbID, TvdbID, TvMazeID                 string
	Edition                                          string

	SeriesTitle string
	SeriesYear  int
	Season      int
	Episodes    []int      // sorted ascending, len >= 1
	Absolute    []int      // parallel to Episodes; nil when not anime
	EpisodeTitle string
	AirDate     *time.Time
	Special     bool

	// Music (Lidarr). Album/audiobook release year reuses the shared Year
	// field above -- Lidarr's and Readarr's own token grammars both spell
	// it "{Release Year}" too (note §A2 lines 94, 99), the same text
	// Radarr uses for a movie's year, so one Context field serves all
	// three rather than three same-named tokens each reading a different
	// field depending on kind.
	ArtistName, ArtistMbID, AlbumTitle, AlbumMbID, TrackTitle string
	Track, Disc                                               int
	MediumFormat                                              string

	// Book / audiobook (Readarr)
	AuthorName, BookTitle, BookSeries, BookSeriesPosition, Narrator string
	PartNumber, PartCount                                          int

	// Comic (Kavita/Komga convention)
	ComicSeriesTitle, IssueNumber string

	// Shared release descriptors
	Quality       commonv1.Quality
	Revision      commonv1.Revision
	MediaInfo     commonv1.MediaInfo
	ReleaseGroup  string
	CustomFormats []string
	OriginalFilename string
}

func (e Engine) Render(template string, c Context) (string, error)

// The nine methods named verbatim in spec §7.
func (e Engine) MovieFolder(c Context) (string, error)
func (e Engine) MovieFile(c Context) (string, error)
func (e Engine) SeriesFolder(c Context) (string, error)
func (e Engine) SeasonFolder(c Context) (string, error) // c.Season == 0 -> dialect-specific specials name
func (e Engine) EpisodeFile(c Context) (string, error)  // picks standard/anime/daily internally: len(c.Absolute)>0 -> anime; c.AirDate != nil -> daily; else standard
func (e Engine) TrackFile(c Context) (string, error)    // includes the album-folder segment (Lidarr convention: track format is album-relative)
func (e Engine) BookFile(c Context) (string, error)      // includes the book-title segment under the author folder (Readarr convention)
func (e Engine) AudiobookFile(c Context) (string, error) // full note-quoted AudiobookFolderFormat, §Disagreement 3
func (e Engine) IssueFile(c Context) (string, error)     // includes the issue segment under the comic-series folder (Kavita/Komga: one folder per series)

// dispatching entry points, additive to the nine spec-named methods above
// (never a replacement -- every one of the nine stays public and unchanged).

//   BuildFile(author|book) -> BookFile
//   BuildFile(audiobook)  -> AudiobookFile
//   BuildFile(comic|issue) -> IssueFile
//   BuildFile(series|artist) -> "", ErrNoFile (container kinds, no single file)
func (e Engine) BuildFolder(kind commonv1.MediaKind, c Context) (string, error)
func (e Engine) BuildFile(kind commonv1.MediaKind, c Context) (string, error)

// ---- Sanitising ----

type SanitizeOptions struct {
	ReplaceIllegal    bool // true: map each illegal char to a safe substitute; false: delete it

}

	DefaultMaxTotalBytes     = 4096 // Linux PATH_MAX

func DefaultSanitizeOptions() SanitizeOptions
```

Run: `go test ./pkg/naming/... -run TestRender -v`

Expected failure: `pkg/naming` does not exist — compile error `no required module provides package github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/naming`.

Implement `pkg/naming/doc.go`, `pkg/naming/errors.go`, `pkg/naming/context.go` (the `Dialect`/`ColonReplacement`/`MultiEpisodeStyle`/`Token*`/`Config`/`Engine`/`NewEngine`/`Context` declarations from Produces, GPL header on every file), and `pkg/naming/render.go`:
```go
package naming

import (
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
)

var tokenRe = regexp.MustCompile(`\{([^{}]*)\}`)

func (e Engine) Render(tmpl string, c Context) (string, error) {
	var errOut error
	out := tokenRe.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(raw string) string {
		if errOut != nil {
			return raw
		}
		prefix, name, suffix := splitWrapper(raw[1 : len(raw)-1])
		base, pad, trunc := splitModifier(name)
		fn, ok := tokenFuncs[normalizeTokenName(base)]
		if !ok {
			errOut = fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUnknownToken, base)
			return raw
		}
		val := fn(c, pad, trunc)
		if val == "" {
			return ""
		}
		return prefix + val + suffix
	})
	if errOut != nil {
		return "", errOut
	}
	return out, nil
}

func splitWrapper(spec string) (prefix, name, suffix string) {
	name = spec
	if len(name) > 0 {
		switch name[0] {
		case '-', '[', '(', ' ':
			prefix, name = string(name[0]), name[1:]
		}
	}
	if len(name) > 0 {
		switch name[len(name)-1] {
		case ']', ')':
			suffix, name = string(name[len(name)-1]), name[:len(name)-1]
		}
	}
	return prefix, name, suffix
}

func splitModifier(name string) (base string, pad, trunc int) {
	i := lastColon(name)
	if i < 0 {
		return name, 0, 0
	}
	mod := name[i+1:]
	if mod != "" && allZero(mod) {
		return name[:i], len(mod), 0
	}
	if n, err := strconv.Atoi(mod); err == nil && n > 0 {
		return name[:i], 0, n
	}
	return name, 0, 0
}

// tokenFuncs is grown by every later step; this step seeds it with the
// three tokens Step 1's test needs.
var tokenFuncs = map[string]func(c Context, pad, trunc int) string{
	"movie title":  func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return c.Title },
	"release year": func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return yearString(c.Year) },
}
```
Add small helpers `lastColon`, `allZero`, `yearString`, `normalizeTokenName` (lower-cases and trims) to `render.go`.

Implement: add to `tokenFuncs`:
```go
"season":  func(c Context, pad, _ int) string { return padInt(c.Season, pad) },
"episode": func(c Context, pad, _ int) string { return padInt(firstOr(c.Episodes), pad) },
"absolute": func(c Context, pad, _ int) string { return padInt(firstOr(c.Absolute), pad) },

```
`padInt(n, width int) string` uses `fmt.Sprintf("%0*d", width, n)` when `width > 0`, else `strconv.Itoa(n)`. `truncate(s string, n int) string` is rune-safe (`[]rune(s)[:n]` guarded by `n <= 0 || len([]rune(s)) <= n`). `firstOr(xs []int) int` returns `xs[0]` or `0`. `cleanTitle` is a forward reference to Step 4 — stub it in this step as `func cleanTitle(s string) string { return s }` in `title.go` (created now, filled in Step 4) so this step compiles standalone.

Implement `pkg/naming/title.go` in full:
```go
package naming

import "strings"

var apostropheStripper = strings.NewReplacer("'", "", "’", "")

func cleanTitle(title string) string { return apostropheStripper.Replace(title) }

func titleThe(title string) string {
	const prefix = "The "
	if strings.HasPrefix(title, prefix) {
		return title[len(prefix):] + ", The"
	}
	return title
}

func replaceColon(s string, mode ColonReplacement) string {
	switch mode {
	case ColonDelete:
		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ":", "")
	case ColonDash:
		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ":", "-")
	case ColonSpaceDash:
		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ":", " -")
	case ColonSpaceDashSpace:
		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ":", " - ")
	default: // ColonSmart and the zero value
		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, ": ", " - ")
		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ":", "-")
	}
}
```
Wire colon replacement into `Render`: after `fn(c, pad, trunc)` returns `val` for any of the `"movie title"`, `"movie cleantitle"`, `"movie titlethe"`, `"series title"`, … title-shaped tokens, apply `replaceColon(val, e.Config.ColonReplacement)` — do this centrally by tagging those token entries in `tokenFuncs` with a `colonSensitive bool` (change the map value type to a small struct `{fn func(Context, int, int) string; colonSensitive bool}`) rather than repeating the call at every call site; update Steps 1-3's map literal accordingly (mechanical, no behaviour change for non-title tokens). Add to `tokenFuncs`:
```go
"movie cleantitle": {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return cleanTitle(c.Title) }, colonSensitive: true},
"movie titlethe":   {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return titleThe(c.Title) }, colonSensitive: true},
```
and mark `"movie title"` from Step 1 `colonSensitive: true` too (the test in Step 4 renders `{Movie CleanTitle}`, but the *arr convention applies colon replacement to every title token, not just CleanTitle — verified by the note's "Illegal characters and CleanTitle" section, which discusses colon replacement and CleanTitle together as the same normalisation pass).

Implement `pkg/naming/quality.go`:
```go
package naming

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
)

var sourceDisplay = map[commonv1.Source]string{
	commonv1.SourceUnknown:   "Unknown",
	commonv1.SourceCam:       "CAM",
	commonv1.SourceTelesync:  "TELESYNC",
	commonv1.SourceTelecine:  "TELECINE",
	commonv1.SourceWorkprint: "Workprint",
	commonv1.SourceDVD:       "DVD",
	commonv1.SourceTV:        "HDTV",
	commonv1.SourceWebDL:     "WEBDL",
	commonv1.SourceWebRip:    "WEBRip",
	commonv1.SourceBluray:    "Bluray",
}

func qualityFull(q commonv1.Quality, r commonv1.Revision) string {
	base := sourceDisplay[q.Source]
	if q.Source == commonv1.SourceTV && q.Resolution > 0 && q.Resolution < 720 {
		base = "SDTV"
	}
	switch q.Modifier {
	case commonv1.ModifierRemux:
		base = "Remux"
	case commonv1.ModifierBRDisk:
		base = "BR-DISK"
	}
	name := base
	if q.Resolution > 0 {
		name = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%dp", base, q.Resolution)
	}
	switch {
	case r.Real > 0:
		name += " REAL"
	case r.Repack:
		name += " Repack"
	case r.Version > 1:
		name += " Proper"
	}
	return name
}

var hdrDisplay = map[commonv1.HdrFormat]string{
	commonv1.HdrFormatPQ10:                 "PQ",
	commonv1.HdrFormatHDR10:                "HDR10",
	commonv1.HdrFormatHDR10Plus:            "HDR10+",
	commonv1.HdrFormatHLG10:                "HLG",
	commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVision:          "DV",
	commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHDR10:     "DV HDR10",
	commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionSDR:       "DV",
	commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHLG:       "DV HLG",
	commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHDR10Plus: "DV HDR10+",
}
```
Add to `tokenFuncs`:
```go

"mediainfo videodynamicrangetype": {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return hdrDisplay[c.MediaInfo.Hdr] }},
"edition tags":  {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return c.Edition }},
"custom formats": {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return strings.Join(c.CustomFormats, " ") }},
"release group": {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return c.ReleaseGroup }},
```

Implement `pkg/naming/series.go` (adds the two methods plus `series cleantitlewithoutyear`, `series year`, and the shared `tvdbid` token — already-registered `tmdbid` from Step 2 is reused as-is since the field is shared, per the Context comment above — to `tokenFuncs`):
```go
package naming

import "fmt"

func (e Engine) SeasonFolder(c Context) (string, error) {
	if c.Season == 0 {
		if e.Config.Dialect == DialectKodi {
			return "Specials", nil
		}
		return "Season 00", nil
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("Season %02d", c.Season), nil
}

func (e Engine) SeriesFolder(c Context) (string, error) {
	tmpl := e.overrideOr(TokenSeriesFolder, seriesFolderTemplate(e.Config.Dialect))
	return e.Render(tmpl, c)
}
```
`seriesFolderTemplate(d Dialect) string` returns the per-dialect literal from the Preset table finalised in Step 12 — for this step, hard-code the four strings inline here (Step 12 moves them into `preset.go` without changing behaviour, a refactor covered by that step's own green run):
```go
func seriesFolderTemplate(d Dialect) string {
	switch d {
	case DialectPlex:
		return "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) {tvdb-{TvdbId}}"
	case DialectEmby:
		return "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) [tvdb-{TvdbId}]"
	case DialectKodi:
		return "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year})"
	default: // Jellyfin
		return "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) [tvdbid-{TvdbId}]"
	}
}
```
Add to `tokenFuncs` (the `tvdbid` entry is not colon-sensitive — ids never carry titles' punctuation; `series cleantitlewithoutyear` is, since it renders `c.SeriesTitle` through the same `cleanTitle`/colon-replacement pass as `movie cleantitle`):
```go
"series cleantitlewithoutyear": {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return cleanTitle(c.SeriesTitle) }, colonSensitive: true},
"series year":                  {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return yearString(c.SeriesYear) }},
"tvdbid":                       {fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { return c.TvdbID }},
```
`e.overrideOr(key, fallback string) string` looks up `e.Config.Overrides[key]`, returning `fallback` when absent/empty — add this small helper to `render.go` now (used again from Step 7 onward).

(`{episodeRange}` is an internal-only token, deliberately not in any *arr table — it exists so this step can test the join function directly through `Render` before `EpisodeFile`'s real template, which never uses `{episodeRange}` itself, needs it; `EpisodeFile`'s standard template instead calls the same Go function directly, exercised by `TestEpisodeFileStandard`. Document this in a one-line comment at the token's registration so a reviewer does not mistake it for a real *arr token.)

Run: `go test ./pkg/naming/... -run 'TestEpisodeFile|TestMultiEpisode' -v`

Expected failure: `Engine.EpisodeFile` undefined; `episoderange`/`episode`/`season` combination token undefined; `episode title`/`episode cleantitle` (already added Step 3) fine.

Implement in `series.go`:
```go
func formatEpisodeRange(season int, episodes []int, style MultiEpisodeStyle) string {
	if len(episodes) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	if len(episodes) == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("S%02dE%02d", season, episodes[0])
	}
	switch style {
	case MultiEpisodeDuplicate:
		parts := make([]string, len(episodes))
		for i, ep := range episodes {
			parts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("S%02dE%02d", season, ep)
		}
		return strings.Join(parts, ".")
	case MultiEpisodeRepeat:
		var b strings.Builder
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "S%02d", season)
		for _, ep := range episodes {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "E%02d", ep)
		}
		return b.String()
	case MultiEpisodeScene:
		var b strings.Builder
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "S%02dE%02d", season, episodes[0])
		for _, ep := range episodes[1:] {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "-E%02d", ep)
		}
		return b.String()
	case MultiEpisodeRange:
		return fmt.Sprintf("S%02dE%02d-%02d", season, episodes[0], episodes[len(episodes)-1])
	case MultiEpisodePrefixedRange:
		return fmt.Sprintf("S%02dE%02d-E%02d", season, episodes[0], episodes[len(episodes)-1])
	default: // MultiEpisodeExtend and the zero value
		var b strings.Builder
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "S%02dE%02d", season, episodes[0])
		for _, ep := range episodes[1:] {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "-%02d", ep)
		}
		return b.String()
	}
}

func (e Engine) EpisodeFile(c Context) (string, error) {
	key, tmpl := TokenEpisodeFile, episodeFileStandardTemplate
	switch {
	case len(c.Absolute) > 0:
		key, tmpl = TokenAnimeFile, episodeFileAnimeTemplate
	case c.AirDate != nil:
		key, tmpl = TokenDailyFile, episodeFileDailyTemplate
	}
	return e.Render(e.overrideOr(key, tmpl), c)
}
```
**A design gap surfaces here, fix it now:** `tokenFuncs` as built in Steps 1-6 is a package-level `map[string]tokenEntry` of closures that only ever see `(c Context, pad, trunc int)` — none of them close over `e`, because none of them needed `e.Config` before now. `formatEpisodeRange` needs `e.Config.MultiEpisodeStyle`, which a package-level map entry cannot reach. Rather than rebuild the whole map per `Engine` (extra allocation on every `Render` call, and every earlier entry would need touching for no reason), give `"episoderange"` (and Step 8's `"absoluterange"`) a `switch` case in `Render` itself, checked *before* the `tokenFuncs` lookup:
```go
func (e Engine) Render(tmpl string, c Context) (string, error) {
	var errOut error
	out := tokenRe.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(raw string) string {
		if errOut != nil {
			return raw
		}
		prefix, name, suffix := splitWrapper(raw[1 : len(raw)-1])
		base, pad, trunc := splitModifier(name)
		key := normalizeTokenName(base)

		var val string
		switch key {
		case "episoderange":
			val = formatEpisodeRange(c.Season, c.Episodes, e.Config.MultiEpisodeStyle)
		default:
			entry, ok := tokenFuncs[key]
			if !ok {
				errOut = fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUnknownToken, base)
				return raw
			}
			val = entry.fn(c, pad, trunc)
			if entry.colonSensitive {
				val = replaceColon(val, e.Config.ColonReplacement)
			}
		}
		if val == "" {
			return ""
		}
		return prefix + val + suffix
	})
	if errOut != nil {
		return "", errOut
	}
	return out, nil
}
```
This replaces Step 1's `Render` body wholesale (Steps 2-6's `tokenFuncs` map entries are untouched; only the dispatch function around them changes) and is the point where Step 4's `colonSensitive` field and this step's `switch` both land in their final shape — no further `Render` restructuring happens after this step.

Implement in `series.go`:
```go
const (
	episodeFileStandardTemplate = "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) - S{season:00}E{episode:00} - {Episode CleanTitle:90} {[Quality Full]}{-Release Group}"
	episodeFileAnimeTemplate    = "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) - S{season:00}E{episode:00} - {absolute:000} - {Episode CleanTitle:90} {[Quality Full]}{-Release Group}"
	episodeFileDailyTemplate    = "{Series CleanTitleWithoutYear} ({Series Year}) - {Air-Date} - {Episode CleanTitle:90} {[Quality Full]}{-Release Group}"
)

func formatAbsoluteRange(episodes, absolute []int, style MultiEpisodeStyle) string {
	if len(absolute) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	if len(absolute) == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%03d", absolute[0])
	}
	switch style {
	case MultiEpisodeRange, MultiEpisodePrefixedRange:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%03d-%03d", absolute[0], absolute[len(absolute)-1])
	case MultiEpisodeDuplicate:
		parts := make([]string, len(absolute))
		for i, a := range absolute {
			parts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%03d", a)
		}
		return strings.Join(parts, ".")
	default: // extend, repeat, scene: dash-joined list
		parts := make([]string, len(absolute))
		for i, a := range absolute {
			parts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%03d", a)
		}
		return strings.Join(parts, "-")
	}
}
```
Add `"air-date"` as an ordinary `tokenFuncs` map entry (`{fn: func(c Context, _, _ int) string { if c.AirDate == nil { return "" }; return c.AirDate.Format("2006-01-02") }}` — it only reads `c`, so it needs no `e.Config` and does not need the `switch` treatment). `"absoluterange"` does need `e.Config` (the `MultiEpisodeStyle`, same reason `"episoderange"` did in Step 7), so it gets a second `case` next to `"episoderange"` in `Render`'s `switch key` block: `case "absoluterange": val = formatAbsoluteRange(c.Episodes, c.Absolute, e.Config.MultiEpisodeStyle)`.

```go
package naming_test

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/naming"
)

type dialectGolden struct {
	Dialect      string `json:"dialect"`
	MovieFolder  string `json:"movieFolder"`
	MovieFile    string `json:"movieFile"`
	SeriesFolder string `json:"seriesFolder"`
}

func TestDialectGoldens(t *testing.T) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile("../../testdata/naming/dialects.json")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var goldens []dialectGolden
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, &goldens))
	require.NotEmpty(t, goldens)

	movie := naming.Context{
		Title: "The Matrix", Year: 1999, TmdbID: "603",
		Quality: commonv1.Quality{Source: commonv1.SourceBluray, Resolution: 2160},
		Revision: commonv1.Revision{Version: 1}, ReleaseGroup: "RlsGrp",
	}
	series := naming.Context{SeriesTitle: "The Series Title!", SeriesYear: 2010, TvdbID: "153021"}

	for _, g := range goldens {
		t.Run(g.Dialect, func(t *testing.T) {
			e := naming.NewEngine(naming.Config{Dialect: naming.Dialect(g.Dialect)})
			mf, err := e.MovieFolder(movie)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			require.Equal(t, g.MovieFolder, mf)

			mF, err := e.MovieFile(movie)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			require.Equal(t, g.MovieFile, mF)

			sf, err := e.SeriesFolder(series)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			require.Equal(t, g.SeriesFolder, sf)
		})
	}
}

func TestOverridesTakePrecedenceOverDialectPreset(t *testing.T) {
	e := naming.NewEngine(naming.Config{
		Dialect:   naming.DialectJellyfin,
		Overrides: map[string]string{naming.TokenMovieFolder: "{Movie Title} only"},
	})
	got, err := e.MovieFolder(naming.Context{Title: "Heat"})

	require.Equal(t, "Heat only", got)
```

```go
package naming

import (
	"fmt"
	"path"

	commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
)

const movieFileTemplate = "{Movie CleanTitle} ({Release Year}) - {[Quality Full]}{-Release Group}"

func movieFolderTemplate(d Dialect) string {
	switch d {
	case DialectPlex:
		return "{Movie CleanTitle} ({Release Year}) {tmdb-{TmdbId}}"
	case DialectEmby:
		return "{Movie CleanTitle} ({Release Year}) [tmdb-{TmdbId}]"
	case DialectKodi:
		return "{Movie CleanTitle} ({Release Year})"
	default:
		return "{Movie CleanTitle} ({Release Year}) [tmdbid-{TmdbId}]"
	}
}

func (e Engine) MovieFolder(c Context) (string, error) {
	return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenMovieFolder, movieFolderTemplate(e.Config.Dialect)), c)
}

func (e Engine) MovieFile(c Context) (string, error) {
	return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenMovieFile, movieFileTemplate), c)
}

func (e Engine) overrideOr(key, fallback string) string {
	if v, ok := e.Config.Overrides[key]; ok && v != "" {
		return v
	}
	return fallback
}

func (e Engine) BuildFolder(kind commonv1.MediaKind, c Context) (string, error) {
	switch kind {
	case commonv1.MediaKindMovie:
		return e.MovieFolder(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindSeries:
		return e.SeriesFolder(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindEpisode:
		sf, err := e.SeriesFolder(c)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		snf, err := e.SeasonFolder(c)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return path.Join(sf, snf), nil
	case commonv1.MediaKindArtist:
		return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenArtistFolder, "{Artist Name}"), c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindAlbum:
		artist, err := e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenArtistFolder, "{Artist Name}"), c)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		album, err := e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenAlbumFolder, "{Album Title} ({Release Year})"), c)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return path.Join(artist, album), nil
	case commonv1.MediaKindAuthor, commonv1.MediaKindBook:
		return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenAuthorFolder, "{Author Name}"), c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindAudiobook:
		return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenAudiobookFolder, audiobookFolderTemplate), c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindComic, commonv1.MediaKindIssue:
		return e.Render(e.overrideOr(TokenComicFolder, "{Comic Series Title}"), c)
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNoFolder, kind)
	}
}

func (e Engine) BuildFile(kind commonv1.MediaKind, c Context) (string, error) {
	switch kind {
	case commonv1.MediaKindMovie:
		return e.MovieFile(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindEpisode:
		return e.EpisodeFile(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindAlbum:
		return e.TrackFile(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindAuthor, commonv1.MediaKindBook:
		return e.BookFile(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindAudiobook:
		return e.AudiobookFile(c)
	case commonv1.MediaKindComic, commonv1.MediaKindIssue:
		return e.IssueFile(c)
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNoFile, kind)
	}
}

const audiobookFolderTemplate = "{Author Name}/{Book Series}/{Book SeriesPosition} - {Release Year} - {Book Title}{ Narrator}"
```
`seriesFolderTemplate` (Step 6) stays in `series.go`; this step does not move it (avoid an unnecessary diff across two files for one commit — noted here so the reviewer does not expect a `series.go` change in this step's commit).

Expected failure: `naming.SanitizePath`/`naming.SanitizeOptions`/`naming.DefaultSanitizeOptions` undefined.

Implement `pkg/naming/sanitize.go`:
```go
package naming

import "strings"

const (
	DefaultMaxComponentBytes = 255
	DefaultMaxTotalBytes     = 4096
)

type SanitizeOptions struct {
	ReplaceIllegal    bool
	IsPath            bool
	MaxComponentBytes int
	MaxTotalBytes     int
}

func DefaultSanitizeOptions() SanitizeOptions {
	return SanitizeOptions{ReplaceIllegal: true, IsPath: true, MaxComponentBytes: DefaultMaxComponentBytes, MaxTotalBytes: DefaultMaxTotalBytes}
}

// illegalReplacements is this task's stated substitution table -- the note
// (§A2, "Illegal characters and CleanTitle") verifies the illegal-character
// set (: \ / > < ? * | ") but not what each one becomes, so this mapping is
// Clustarr's own convention, chosen to stay readable rather than lossy.
var illegalReplacements = map[rune]string{
	':': "-", '\\': "-", '/': "-", '>': "", '<': "", '"': "'", '|': "-", '?': "", '*': "",
}

func SanitizePath(s string, opts SanitizeOptions) string {
	if opts.MaxComponentBytes <= 0 {
		opts.MaxComponentBytes = DefaultMaxComponentBytes
	}
	if opts.MaxTotalBytes <= 0 {
		opts.MaxTotalBytes = DefaultMaxTotalBytes
	}
	segments := []string{s}
	if opts.IsPath {
		segments = strings.Split(s, "/")
	}
	for i, seg := range segments {
		segments[i] = sanitizeComponent(seg, opts)
	}
	sep := ""
	if opts.IsPath {
		sep = "/"
	}
	out := strings.Join(segments, sep)
	return capTotal(out, opts.MaxTotalBytes, opts.IsPath)
}

func sanitizeComponent(s string, opts SanitizeOptions) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range s {
		if r == '/' && opts.IsPath {
			b.WriteRune(r) // a stray '/' inside what should be one segment: keep, caller's Split already segmented on real ones
			continue
		}
		repl, illegal := illegalReplacements[r]
		switch {
		case !illegal:
			b.WriteRune(r)
		case opts.ReplaceIllegal:
			b.WriteString(repl)
		}
	}
	out := strings.TrimRight(b.String(), ". ")
	return truncateBytes(out, opts.MaxComponentBytes)
}

func truncateBytes(s string, max int) string {
	if len(s) <= max {
		return s
	}
	return string([]rune(s)[:runesForBytes(s, max)])
}
```
Add `runesForBytes(s string, max int) int` (walk runes accumulating `utf8.RuneLen`, stop before exceeding `max`) and `capTotal(s string, max int, isPath bool) string` (when `len(s) <= max`, return unchanged; else, for `isPath`, re-truncate only the last `/`-segment down to fit, for `!isPath` truncate the whole string via `truncateBytes`) to `sanitize.go`.

Expected pass: all five green. Double check `TestSanitizePathReplacesIllegalCharacters`'s expected string by hand against `illegalReplacements` before trusting it blind — the walkthrough in this task's research (Read First) computed it character-by-character; if the test fails on this specific string, the bug is almost always a copy-paste mismatch between the *expected* literal and the *input* literal, not the sanitiser logic.

Run: `go test ./pkg/naming/... -run TestSanitizePathCaps -v`

Expected failure: first case likely already passes if Step 14's `truncateBytes` is correct (confirm, don't assume — run it before writing new code); the second exercises `capTotal`'s path-aware branch, which Step 14 stubbed with a plausible-but-unverified implementation. If `capTotal` under-implements the "only shrink the last segment" rule, this is where it shows: `len(got)` will exceed 4096 or the `"movies/"` prefix will be gone.

Implement: fix/complete `capTotal` in `sanitize.go`:
```go
func capTotal(s string, max int, isPath bool) string {
	if len(s) <= max || !isPath {
		return truncateBytes(s, max)
	}
	i := strings.LastIndexByte(s, '/')
	if i < 0 {
		return truncateBytes(s, max)
	}
	head, tail := s[:i+1], s[i+1:]
	room := max - len(head)
	if room <= 0 {
		return truncateBytes(s, max) // pathological: head alone already over budget
	}
	return head + truncateBytes(tail, room)
}
```

Implement `pkg/naming/subtitle.go`:
```go
package naming

import (
	"path"
	"strings"
)

func SubtitlePath(mediaPath, lang string, forced, hi bool) string {
	ext := path.Ext(mediaPath)
	stem := strings.TrimSuffix(mediaPath, ext)
	tag := ""
	switch {
	case forced:
		tag = ".forced"
	case hi:
		tag = ".sdh"
	}
	return stem + "." + strings.ToLower(lang) + tag + ".srt"
}
```

Implement `pkg/naming/recycle.go`:
```go
package naming

import (
	"fmt"
	"path"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

func RecycleBinPath(binRoot, rootFolderPath, itemPath string, now time.Time) (string, error) {
	rel := strings.TrimPrefix(itemPath, rootFolderPath)
	if rel == itemPath || (rel != "" && rel[0] != '/') {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %q under %q", ErrNotUnderRoot, itemPath, rootFolderPath)
	}
	return path.Join(binRoot, now.Format("2006-01-02"), rel), nil
}
```

**Interfaces — Produces:**

`gopkg.in/vansante/go-ffprobe.v2`'s own `ffprobe.Format`, `ffprobe.Stream` and `ffprobe.Chapter` are re-exported unchanged inside `Raw` (see the note on this below) — a caller of `Raw` (`pkg/transcode.Planner.Plan`) imports that module too.

```go
package mediainfo // github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/mediainfo

// Raw is the unabridged ffprobe result for one file: every stream, the
// container format and chapters, plus the HDR/Dolby-Vision and colour
// detail api/common/v1alpha1.MediaInfo has no field for.
type Raw struct {
	Format   *ffprobe.Format
	Streams  []*ffprobe.Stream
	Chapters []*ffprobe.Chapter

	ColorPrimaries string // from the second (frame-level) ffprobe call
	ColorTransfer  string
	ColorSpace     string
	ColorRange     string

	Dovi         *DoviRecord // nil when the source has no Dolby Vision RPU
	HasHDR10Plus bool

	MasterDisplay string // pre-formatted for libx265 -x265-params master-display=...
	MaxCLL        string // pre-formatted for libx265 -x265-params max-cll=...
}

// DoviRecord is the primary video stream's "DOVI configuration record"
// side data (libavutil/side_data.c field names).
type DoviRecord struct {
	VersionMajor, VersionMinor       int32
	Profile, Level                   int32
	RPUPresent, ELPresent, BLPresent bool
	BLSignalCompatibilityID          int32
	MDCompression                    string
}

// ErrTooSmall is returned by MovieHash for files under 128 KiB.
var ErrTooSmall error

func Probe(ctx context.Context, path string) (*commonv1.MediaInfo, *Raw, error)
func ClassifyHDR(raw *Raw) commonv1.HdrFormat
func ProbeHash(path string, size int64, mtime time.Time) string
func MovieHash(path string) (string, error)

// VideoDynamicRangeType renders hdr as pkg/naming's
// {MediaInfo VideoDynamicRangeType} token expects ("HDR10", "DV HDR10", ...).
func VideoDynamicRangeType(hdr commonv1.HdrFormat) string

// AudioChannelsString renders a channel layout as the *arr display string
// ("5.1", "7.1", "2.0"), for pkg/naming's {MediaInfo AudioChannels} token.
func AudioChannelsString(channelLayout string, channels int32) string

// ResolutionFromDimensions buckets a frame size into 480/576/720/1080/2160.
func ResolutionFromDimensions(width, height int32) int32
```

**Why `Raw` carries the ffprobe types verbatim, and why some task-brief fields aren't on `MediaInfo`:** the design brief for this task asked for level, colour primaries/transfer/matrix, master-display/max-cll strings, audio channel-layout and a forced flag, and a full chapter list — none of which exist on the real generated `api/common/v1alpha1.MediaInfo` (see **Read first** above), and the spec's own `pkg/mediainfo` signature returns exactly `(*common.MediaInfo, *Raw, error)` with the comment "Raw keeps DOVI record + MDCV/CLL" — not a third, richer struct. This task resolves the conflict in the spec's favour (CLAUDE.md: "the spec is authoritative for names, fields and behaviour"): every field the CRD type actually has is mapped onto `*commonv1.MediaInfo`; everything else (level, colour tags, master-display/max-cll, the full per-chapter list, per-stream detail beyond what the CRD models) lives on the exported `Raw`, which `pkg/transcode.Planner.Plan(mi *common.MediaInfo, raw *mediainfo.Raw, hw string)` reads directly.

  ```go
  package mediainfo

  import (
  	"crypto/sha1"
  	"encoding/hex"
  	"fmt"
  	"time"
  )

  // ProbeHash is sha1(path|size|mtime), matching
  // api/catalog/v1alpha1.MediaFileStatus.ProbeHash's doc comment: a change
  // in any of the three makes downstream services (transcode compliance,
  // subtitle sidecar rescans) replan.
  func ProbeHash(path string, size int64, mtime time.Time) string {
  	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("%s|%d|%d", path, size, mtime.UnixNano())))
  	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
  }
  ```

  ```go
  import (

  func TestMovieHash(t *testing.T) {
  	dir := t.TempDir()

  	// All-zero file, exactly 2*osChunk bytes: first and last 64 KiB span
  	// the whole file with no overlap and no gap, so the expected hash is
  	// hand-computable: sum = uint64(size) + 0 + 0 = 131072 = 0x20000.
  	zeros := filepath.Join(dir, "zeros.bin")
  	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(zeros, make([]byte, 2*osChunk), 0o644))
  	got, err := MovieHash(zeros)
  	require.NoError(t, err)
  	assert.Equal(t, "0000000000020000", got)

  	// All-0x01 file, same size: every little-endian uint64 word is
  	// 0x0101010101010101; sum = size + 16384*word, mod 2^64.
  	ones := filepath.Join(dir, "ones.bin")
  	buf := make([]byte, 2*osChunk)
  	for i := range buf {
  		buf[i] = 0x01
  	}
  	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(ones, buf, 0o644))
  	got, err = MovieHash(ones)
  	require.NoError(t, err)
  	assert.Equal(t, "4040404040424000", got)

  	tiny := filepath.Join(dir, "tiny.bin")
  	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(tiny, make([]byte, 100), 0o644))
  	_, err = MovieHash(tiny)
  	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrTooSmall)
  }
  ```
  Both hex vectors above are independently computed (`(size + N*word) mod 2**64` in Python) against docs/research/subtitles.md §4.4's algorithm, not against this task's own implementation — reproduce them yourself before committing:
  ```bash
  python3 -c "
  MASK=(1<<64)-1
  print(format(131072 & MASK, '016x'))
  print(format((131072 + (131072//8)*0x0101010101010101) & MASK, '016x'))
  "
  ```

  Run: `go test ./pkg/mediainfo/... -run TestMovieHash -v`
  Expected failure: `undefined: MovieHash`, `undefined: osChunk`, `undefined: ErrTooSmall`.

  Implement, appending to `pkg/mediainfo/hash.go`:
  ```go
  import (
  	"encoding/binary"
  	"errors"
  	"io"
  	"os"
  )

  // osChunk is the OpenSubtitles moviehash chunk size: the first and last
  // 64 KiB of the file (docs/research/subtitles.md §4.4).
  const osChunk = 64 * 1024

  // ErrTooSmall is returned by MovieHash for files under 2*osChunk (128
  // KiB): docs/research/subtitles.md §4.4 notes the upstream Python
  // reference implementation rejects them outright.
  var ErrTooSmall = errors.New("mediainfo: file smaller than 128 KiB, cannot compute movie hash")

  // MovieHash is OpenSubtitles' moviehash: filesize plus the sum of the
  // first and last 64 KiB read as little-endian uint64 words, wrapping mod
  // 2^64, printed as 16 lowercase hex digits (docs/research/subtitles.md §4.4).
  func MovieHash(path string) (string, error) {
  	f, err := os.Open(path)
  	if err != nil {
  		return "", fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: movie hash: %w", err)
  	}
  	defer f.Close()

  	st, err := f.Stat()
  	if err != nil {
  		return "", fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: movie hash: %w", err)
  	}
  	if st.Size() < 2*osChunk {
  		return "", ErrTooSmall
  	}

  	sum := uint64(st.Size())
  	buf := make([]byte, osChunk)
  	for _, off := range []int64{0, st.Size() - osChunk} {
  		if _, err := f.ReadAt(buf, off); err != nil && err != io.EOF {
  			return "", fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: movie hash: %w", err)
  		}
  		for i := 0; i < osChunk; i += 8 {
  			sum += binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[i:])
  		}
  	}
  	return fmt.Sprintf("%016x", sum), nil
  }
  ```

  Run: `go test ./pkg/mediainfo/... -run 'TestProbeHash|TestMovieHash' -v` — expect `PASS`.

  Run: `go test ./pkg/mediainfo/... -run 'TestBitDepth|TestFrameRate|TestKbps|TestContainer' -v`

  Implement `pkg/mediainfo/classify.go`:
  ```go
  package mediainfo

  import (
  	"path/filepath"
  	"strconv"
  	"strings"
  )

  // bitDepthFromPixFmt returns the video bit depth ffprobe's pix_fmt
  // implies: "yuv420p" -> 8 (the implicit default), "yuv420p10le" -> 10,
  // "...12le" -> 12.
  func bitDepthFromPixFmt(pixFmt string) int32 {
  	switch {
  	case strings.Contains(pixFmt, "12le"), strings.Contains(pixFmt, "12be"):
  		return 12
  	case strings.Contains(pixFmt, "10le"), strings.Contains(pixFmt, "10be"):
  		return 10
  	default:
  		return 8
  	}
  }

  // frameRateMilli parses ffprobe's r_frame_rate ("24/1", "24000/1001")
  // into thousandths of a frame per second (23.976 fps -> 23976), matching
  // api/common/v1alpha1.MediaInfo.FpsMilli's scaled-integer convention.
  func frameRateMilli(rFrameRate string) int32 {
  	num, den, ok := strings.Cut(rFrameRate, "/")
  	if !ok {
  		return 0
  	}
  	n, err1 := strconv.ParseFloat(num, 64)
  	d, err2 := strconv.ParseFloat(den, 64)
  	if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || d == 0 {
  		return 0
  	}
  	return int32(mathRound(n / d * 1000))
  }

  // kbpsFromBitRate parses ffprobe's decimal bit_rate string (bits/second)
  // into whole kilobits/second. Some containers (MKV video streams
  // especially) omit bit_rate entirely; that parses to 0, not an error.
  func kbpsFromBitRate(bitRate string) int32 {
  	v, err := strconv.ParseInt(bitRate, 10, 64)
  	if err != nil {
  		return 0
  	}
  	return int32(v / 1000)
  }

  // containerFromPath derives the container token from the file extension.
  // ffprobe's format_name lists every demuxer alias a container matches
  // ("mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2" for an .mp4), which is not usable as-is.
  func containerFromPath(path string) string {
  	return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimPrefix(filepath.Ext(path), "."))
  }
  ```
  `mathRound` is a one-line `math.Round` wrapper added here to keep the `math` import next to its only use:
  ```go
  import "math"

  func mathRound(f float64) float64 { return math.Round(f) }
  ```
  (Fold this into the `frameRateMilli` file directly — a separate helper is only to keep the diff readable in this plan; the implementer may just call `math.Round` inline.)

  Implement `pkg/mediainfo/mediainfo.go`:
  ```go
  // Package mediainfo wraps ffprobe to produce the api/common/v1alpha1
  // MediaInfo the MediaFile status carries, plus the richer Raw detail
  // (the full ffprobe result, the Dolby Vision configuration record, and
  // pre-formatted libx265 master-display/max-cll strings) that
  // api/common/v1alpha1.MediaInfo has no room for and pkg/transcode's
  // Planner needs. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-clustarr-design.md
  // §7 and docs/research/transcode.md §2.
  package mediainfo

  import (
  	ffprobe "gopkg.in/vansante/go-ffprobe.v2"
  )

  // Raw is the unabridged ffprobe result for one file: every stream, the
  // container format and chapters, plus the HDR/Dolby-Vision and colour
  // detail the CRD-facing MediaInfo cannot hold. pkg/transcode.Planner.Plan
  // takes Raw as its second argument; catalogarr's MediaFile status only
  // ever sees the mapped MediaInfo Probe returns alongside it.
  type Raw struct {
  	Format   *ffprobe.Format
  	Streams  []*ffprobe.Stream
  	Chapters []*ffprobe.Chapter

  	// ColorPrimaries, ColorTransfer, ColorSpace and ColorRange are read
  	// from the first decoded frame (the second ffprobe call, added in
  	// Step 5), more reliable than the stream-level tags for some
  	// encoders -- docs/research/transcode.md §2.1.
  	ColorPrimaries string
  	ColorTransfer  string
  	ColorSpace     string
  	ColorRange     string

  	// Dovi is the primary video stream's "DOVI configuration record" side
  	// data, nil when the source carries no Dolby Vision RPU.
  	Dovi *DoviRecord

  	// HasHDR10Plus is true when the first frame carries "HDR Dynamic
  	// Metadata SMPTE2094-40 (HDR10+)" side data. Set in Step 5.
  	HasHDR10Plus bool

  	// MasterDisplay and MaxCLL are pre-formatted for libx265's
  	// -x265-params (docs/research/transcode.md §2.2's handle_mdcv
  	// conversion). Set in Step 5; empty until then.
  	MasterDisplay string
  	MaxCLL        string
  }

  // DoviRecord is the "DOVI configuration record" stream side data
  // (libavutil/side_data.c field names; docs/research/transcode.md §2.2).
  type DoviRecord struct {
  	VersionMajor, VersionMinor       int32
  	Profile, Level                   int32
  	RPUPresent, ELPresent, BLPresent bool
  	BLSignalCompatibilityID          int32
  	MDCompression                    string
  }

  // buildRaw copies pd's streams/format/chapters onto Raw and extracts the
  // primary video stream's Dolby Vision record. Step 5 adds the
  // frame-level merge on top.
  func buildRaw(pd *ffprobe.ProbeData) *Raw {
  	raw := &Raw{Format: pd.Format, Streams: pd.Streams, Chapters: pd.Chapters}
  	if v := pd.FirstVideoStream(); v != nil {
  		raw.Dovi = parseDoviRecord(v.SideDataList)
  	}
  	return raw
  }
  ```

  And `pkg/mediainfo/ffprobe.go`:
  ```go
  package mediainfo

  import (
  	ffprobe "gopkg.in/vansante/go-ffprobe.v2"
  )

  // parseDoviRecord extracts the "DOVI configuration record" side data
  // from a video stream's side data list. go-ffprobe.v2 v2.3.1 has no
  // typed struct for this side_data_type, so it decodes as
  // *ffprobe.SideDataUnknown (a map[string]interface{} in disguise);
  // Tags(*unknown) recovers the GetInt/GetString accessors.
  func parseDoviRecord(list ffprobe.SideDataList) *DoviRecord {
  	data, err := list.FindSideData("DOVI configuration record")
  	if err != nil {
  		return nil
  	}
  	unknown, ok := data.(*ffprobe.SideDataUnknown)
  	if !ok {
  		return nil
  	}
  	tags := ffprobe.Tags(*unknown)
  	geti := func(k string) int32 {
  		v, _ := tags.GetInt(k)
  		return int32(v)
  	}
  	compression, _ := tags.GetString("dv_md_compression")
  	return &DoviRecord{
  		VersionMajor:            geti("dv_version_major"),
  		VersionMinor:            geti("dv_version_minor"),
  		Profile:                 geti("dv_profile"),
  		Level:                   geti("dv_level"),
  		RPUPresent:              geti("rpu_present_flag") != 0,
  		ELPresent:               geti("el_present_flag") != 0,
  		BLPresent:               geti("bl_present_flag") != 0,
  		BLSignalCompatibilityID: geti("dv_bl_signal_compatibility_id"),
  		MDCompression:           compression,
  	}
  }
  ```

  Implement, appending to `pkg/mediainfo/ffprobe.go`:
  ```go
  import (
  	"bytes"
  	"context"
  	"encoding/json"
  	"fmt"
  	"math"
  	"os/exec"
  )

  // frameProbeData is the shape of the second ffprobe call's JSON.
  // go-ffprobe.v2's ProbeData has no field for ffprobe's "frames" array, so
  // this call is issued directly with os/exec (see runFrameProbe) and
  // decoded into this package-local type.
  type frameProbeData struct {
  	Frames []frameEntry `json:"frames"`
  }

  type frameEntry struct {
  	ColorPrimaries string               `json:"color_primaries"`
  	ColorTransfer  string               `json:"color_transfer"`
  	ColorSpace     string               `json:"color_space"`
  	ColorRange     string               `json:"color_range"`
  	SideDataList   ffprobe.SideDataList `json:"side_data_list"`
  }

  // hdr10PlusSideDataType is the frame-level side_data_type ffprobe prints
  // for SMPTE 2094-40 dynamic metadata (docs/research/transcode.md §2.2's
  // side-data table).
  const hdr10PlusSideDataType = "HDR Dynamic Metadata SMPTE2094-40 (HDR10+)"

  // mergeFrame layers the second ffprobe call's first-frame colour tags and
  // HDR side data onto raw. docs/research/transcode.md §2.1: "HDR static
  // metadata + real colour tags come from the first decoded frame."
  func mergeFrame(raw *Raw, frames frameProbeData) {
  	if len(frames.Frames) == 0 {
  		return
  	}
  	f := frames.Frames[0]
  	raw.ColorPrimaries = f.ColorPrimaries
  	raw.ColorTransfer = f.ColorTransfer
  	raw.ColorSpace = f.ColorSpace
  	raw.ColorRange = f.ColorRange

  	for _, sd := range f.SideDataList {
  		switch sd.Type {
  		case ffprobe.SideDataTypeMasteringDisplayMetadata:
  			if m, ok := sd.Data.(*ffprobe.SideDataMasteringDisplayMetadata); ok {
  				raw.MasterDisplay = formatMasterDisplay(m)
  			}
  		case ffprobe.SideDataTypeContentLightLevel:
  			if c, ok := sd.Data.(*ffprobe.SideDataContentLightLevel); ok {
  				raw.MaxCLL = formatMaxCLL(c)
  			}
  		case hdr10PlusSideDataType:
  			raw.HasHDR10Plus = true
  		}
  	}
  }

  // formatMasterDisplay renders m exactly as libavcodec/libx265.c's
  // handle_mdcv does (docs/research/transcode.md §2.2): chromaticity as
  // integers over 50000, luminance as (max,min) in units of 0.0001 cd/m2.
  func formatMasterDisplay(m *ffprobe.SideDataMasteringDisplayMetadata) string {
  	return fmt.Sprintf("G(%d,%d)B(%d,%d)R(%d,%d)WP(%d,%d)L(%d,%d)",
  		round(m.GreenX*50000), round(m.GreenY*50000),
  		round(m.BlueX*50000), round(m.BlueY*50000),
  		round(m.RedX*50000), round(m.RedY*50000),
  		round(m.WhitePointX*50000), round(m.WhitePointY*50000),
  		round(m.MaxLuminance*10000), round(m.MinLuminance*10000))
  }

  func formatMaxCLL(c *ffprobe.SideDataContentLightLevel) string {
  	return fmt.Sprintf("%d,%d", c.MaxContent, c.MaxAverage)
  }

  func round(f ffprobe.FlexFloat) int64 {
  	return int64(math.Round(float64(f)))
  }

  // runFrameProbe issues the second ffprobe call: the first decoded
  // frame's colour tags and HDR side data, per docs/research/transcode.md
  // §2.1's second command, verbatim. go-ffprobe.v2 cannot express this
  // call (no Frames field on ProbeData), so it bypasses the library.
  func runFrameProbe(ctx context.Context, path string) (frameProbeData, error) {
  	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "ffprobe",
  		"-v", "error", "-print_format", "json",
  		"-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_frames", "-read_intervals", "%+#1",
  		"-show_entries", "frame=pix_fmt,color_primaries,color_transfer,color_space,color_range,side_data_list",
  		path)
  	var out, stderr bytes.Buffer
  	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &stderr
  	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
  		return frameProbeData{}, fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: ffprobe frame probe: %w: %s", err, stderr.String())
  	}
  	var fd frameProbeData
  	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &fd); err != nil {
  		return frameProbeData{}, fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: parse frame probe json: %w", err)
  	}
  	return fd, nil
  }
  ```
  (`ffprobe` here is the `gopkg.in/vansante/go-ffprobe.v2` import alias already used by `parseDoviRecord` in the same file — one `import` block covers both functions.)

  ```go
  import commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"

  // ClassifyHDR derives the api/common HDR vocabulary from raw's Dolby
  // Vision record and frame-level colour tags, per
  // docs/research/transcode.md §2.3 "Deriving HDRFormat" and §3.5's
  // profile/compat-id table.
  func ClassifyHDR(raw *Raw) commonv1.HdrFormat {
  	if raw == nil {
  		return commonv1.HdrFormatNone
  	}
  	if raw.Dovi != nil {
  		switch raw.Dovi.Profile {
  		case 5:
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVision
  		case 7:
  			// FFmpeg's decoder drops the enhancement layer, so a profile 7
  			// base layer decodes as HDR10 (docs/research/transcode.md §3.5).
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHDR10
  		}
  		switch raw.Dovi.BLSignalCompatibilityID {
  		case 1:
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHDR10
  		case 2:
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionSDR
  		case 4:
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVisionHLG
  		default:
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatDolbyVision
  		}

  	switch {

  		return commonv1.HdrFormatHDR10Plus
  	case raw.ColorTransfer == "smpte2084":
  		if raw.MasterDisplay != "" {
  			return commonv1.HdrFormatHDR10

  		return commonv1.HdrFormatPQ10
  	case raw.ColorTransfer == "arib-std-b67":
  		return commonv1.HdrFormatHLG10
  	default:
  		return commonv1.HdrFormatNone
  	}
  }
  ```

  ```go
  import "fmt"

  // AudioChannelsString renders a channel layout as the *arr display
  // string ("5.1", "7.1", "2.0"). It prefers ffprobe's channel_layout,
  // stripping any positional suffix ("5.1(side)" -> "5.1"; see
  // docs/research/transcode.md §2.2), and falls back to "<channels>.0"
  // when the layout is empty or unrecognized.
  func AudioChannelsString(channelLayout string, channels int32) string {
  	switch channelLayout {
  	case "mono":
  		return "1.0"
  	case "stereo":
  		return "2.0"
  	}
  	if i := strings.IndexByte(channelLayout, '('); i >= 0 {
  		channelLayout = channelLayout[:i]
  	}
  	if channelLayout != "" {
  		return channelLayout
  	}
  	return fmt.Sprintf("%d.0", channels)
  }
  ```

  ```go
  // ResolutionFromDimensions buckets a frame size into the *arr resolution
  // values docs/research/naming.md documents (480, 576, 720, 1080, 2160),
  // banding on height.
  func ResolutionFromDimensions(width, height int32) int32 {
  	h := height
  	if h == 0 && width > 0 {
  		h = width * 9 / 16
  	}
  	switch {
  	case h <= 480:
  		return 480
  	case h <= 576:
  		return 576
  	case h <= 720:
  		return 720
  	case h <= 1080:
  		return 1080
  	default:
  		return 2160
  	}
  }
  ```
