- [ ] **Step 8: implement `Validate`, wire it into `Load`**
```go
//go:embed schema.json
var schemaJSON []byte

var compiledSchema = sync.OnceValues(func() (*jsonschema.Schema, error) {
	doc, err := jsonschema.UnmarshalJSON(bytes.NewReader(schemaJSON))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: parse embedded schema: %w", err)
	}
	c := jsonschema.NewCompiler()
	if err := c.AddResource("schema-v11.json", doc); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: load embedded schema: %w", err)
	}
	return c.Compile("schema-v11.json")
})

func Validate(data []byte) error {
	sch, err := compiledSchema()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	jsonBytes, err := yaml.YAMLToJSON(data)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cardigann: yaml to json: %w", err)
	}
	var v any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(jsonBytes, &v); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cardigann: decode definition json: %w", err)
	}
	if err := sch.Validate(v); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cardigann: schema validation: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}
```
`Load` calls `Validate(data)` first and returns its error unwrapped-but-wrapped-again (`fmt.Errorf("cardigann: %w", err)` is redundant given `Validate` already prefixes — just `return nil, err` on validate failure) before decoding.

- [ ] **Step 18: implement `render` (exported as `RenderForTest` for the test package, or move template_test.go into package `cardigann` — pick the latter: put this one file in package `cardigann` so it can call the unexported `render` directly, and say so in the file's own doc comment for the reviewer)**, the FuncMap, and `ResolveSettings`/`NewConfig`

Go's `text/template` already provides `if`/`else`/`range`/`and`/`or`/`eq`/`ne` — the note's documented dialect (§3.6) needs exactly two additions:
```go
var funcMap = template.FuncMap{
	"join": func(vs []string, sep string) string { return strings.Join(vs, sep) },
	"re_replace": func(value, pattern, repl string) (string, error) {
		re, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("cardigann: re_replace: %w", err)
		}
		return re.ReplaceAllString(value, repl), nil
	},
}

func render(tmplText string, tc *TemplateContext) (string, error) {
	t, err := template.New("cardigann").Funcs(funcMap).Parse(tmplText)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("cardigann: template %q: %w", tmplText, err)
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	if err := t.Execute(&buf, tc); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("cardigann: template exec %q: %w", tmplText, err)
	}
	return buf.String(), nil
}
```
`ResolveSettings` walks `d.Settings`; for `Type == "checkbox"`, output `"true"` when the raw value (or `Default`) is truthy else `""`; for `Type == "select"`, output the raw value verbatim if it is a key in `Options`, else `Default`; for `"text"|"password"`, output raw or `Default`; `"info*"` types are skipped (never appear in the map). Always set `values["sitelink"] = baseURL`. `sprig/v3`'s FuncMap is deliberately **not** merged in — the Produces comment on `Filters` and this section both say why: Cardigann's own template dialect is small and closed, and exposing sprig's ~100 extra functions to a definition author would silently accept syntax no real Prowlarr definition uses (untestable against the corpus) and let a future custom `IndexerDefinition` depend on Clustarr-only template behaviour that breaks compatibility with upstream Cardigann files. (`Masterminds/sprig/v3` stays a pre-added-but-unused dependency for this task; a later task may prove it's needed for something specific — do not add it to `funcMap` speculatively.)

- [ ] **Step 23: implement the dispatcher**

```go
type ResponseType int

const (
	ResponseHTML ResponseType = iota
	ResponseJSON
	ResponseXML
)

type Doc struct {
	rt   ResponseType
	html *goquery.Selection
	json gjson.Result
	xml  *xmlquery.Node
}

func ParseDoc(rt ResponseType, body []byte) (Doc, error) {
	switch rt {
	case ResponseHTML:
		d, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(bytes.NewReader(body))
		if err != nil {
			return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: parse html: %w", err)
		}
		return Doc{rt: rt, html: d.Selection}, nil
	case ResponseJSON:
		if !gjson.ValidBytes(body) {
			return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: invalid json response")
		}
		return Doc{rt: rt, json: gjson.ParseBytes(body)}, nil
	case ResponseXML:
		n, err := xmlquery.Parse(bytes.NewReader(body))
		if err != nil {
			return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: parse xml: %w", err)
		}
		return Doc{rt: rt, xml: n}, nil
	default:
		return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: unknown response type %d", rt)
	}
}

func (d Doc) Select(selector string) (Doc, bool) {
	switch d.rt {
	case ResponseHTML:
		sel := d.html.Find(selector)
		if sel.Length() == 0 {
			return Doc{}, false
		}
		return Doc{rt: d.rt, html: sel}, true
	case ResponseJSON:
		r := d.json.Get(selector)
		if !r.Exists() {
			return Doc{}, false
		}
		return Doc{rt: d.rt, json: r}, true
	case ResponseXML:
		n := xmlquery.FindOne(d.xml, selector)
		if n == nil {
			return Doc{}, false
		}
		return Doc{rt: d.rt, xml: n}, true
	}
	return Doc{}, false
}

func (d Doc) Rows(selector string) []Doc {
	switch d.rt {
	case ResponseHTML:
		var out []Doc
		d.html.Find(selector).Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) { out = append(out, Doc{rt: d.rt, html: s}) })
		return out
	case ResponseJSON:
		var out []Doc
		d.json.Get(selector).ForEach(func(_, v gjson.Result) bool {
			out = append(out, Doc{rt: d.rt, json: v})
			return true
		})
		return out
	case ResponseXML:
		var out []Doc
		for _, n := range xmlquery.Find(d.xml, selector) {
			out = append(out, Doc{rt: d.rt, xml: n})
		}
		return out
	}
	return nil
}

func (d Doc) Text(attribute string) (string, bool) {
	switch d.rt {
	case ResponseHTML:
		if attribute == "" {
			return strings.TrimSpace(d.html.Text()), true
		}
		return d.html.Attr(attribute)
	case ResponseJSON:
		if attribute != "" {
			sub, ok := d.Select(attribute)
			if !ok {
				return "", false
			}
			return sub.Text("")
		}
		if d.json.IsArray() {
			var parts []string
			d.json.ForEach(func(_, v gjson.Result) bool { parts = append(parts, v.String()); return true })
			return strings.Join(parts, ","), true // see note: matches the corpus's plain re_replace use on meta.genres
		}
		return d.json.String(), true
	case ResponseXML:
		if attribute == "" {
			return strings.TrimSpace(d.xml.InnerText()), true
		}
		for _, a := range d.xml.Attr {
			if a.Name.Local == attribute {
				return a.Value, true
			}
		}
		return "", false
	}
	return "", false
}
```
`SelectorBlock.Extract` composes these: `Text` field short-circuits (`render` it as a template and return); else `Select(b.Selector)`, apply `Remove` via `sel.HTML.Find(remove).Remove()` when HTML, read `Text(b.Attribute)`; on no match, return `("", false, nil)` when `b.Optional` (using `*b.Default` when set), else `("", false, nil)` too (the caller — RowsBlock iteration / field mapping in `search.go` — is what turns a non-optional miss into "drop this row", not `Extract` itself, since `Extract` has no notion of "this field is required" beyond what `Optional` already encodes — a required field with `Optional: false` that misses simply also returns `ok=false`, and the caller's contract is: `!ok && !b.Optional` half of the check is redundant given schema `dependentRequired`, drop the row). Apply `Case` (render the matched value, or the `"*"` fallback, or leave raw unchanged when no `Case` map is present) before the `Filters` chain, which runs each filter with `Filters[f.Name](ctx, value, f.Args, tc)` in file order, returning an error on any unknown name (never possible for a schema-validated definition, but a synthetic test definition can exercise it).

The three time-relative filters (`timeago`, `reltime`, `fuzzytime`) all read `tc.Now` (never `time.Now()` directly, for determinism) and return `t.Format(time.RFC3339)`; `dateparse`/`timeparse` (identical implementation — the schema and note both describe them the same way, only the name differs across the Jackett-derived corpus) call `TranslateDateFormat(args[0])` then `time.Parse`, retrying with `strings.ToUpper(value)` when the layout contains `"PM"` and the first parse fails — this is a real gotcha: Go's `"PM"` layout token only matches literal upper-case `AM`/`PM` in the source text, but the 1337x corpus writes lower-case (`"7am"`), so a naive translation silently fails to parse every `htt`-formatted date:
```go
func parseWithLayout(dotnetFormat, value string) (time.Time, error) {
	layout := TranslateDateFormat(dotnetFormat)
	t, err := time.Parse(layout, value)
	if err != nil && strings.Contains(layout, "PM") {
		t, err = time.Parse(layout, strings.ToUpper(value))
	}
	if err != nil {
		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: parse date %q with layout %q: %w", value, layout, err)
	}
	return t, nil
}
```
`validfilename` strips exactly `<>:"/\|?*` (the Windows-reserved set Prowlarr's own filter targets). `diacritics`'s single documented arg is the literal string `"replace"` (no other mode exists in the corpus); implement via `golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm` NFD, strip `unicode.Mn` runes, NFC — **note:** `golang.org/x/text` is not in the pre-add list; if `go build` reports it missing, this is a `NEEDS_CONTEXT` case per the Phase B rules (report the missing module to the controller, do not `go get` it yourself) — the fallback within this task's own scope is a hand-rolled ASCII transliteration table sized to the corpus's actual accented characters (é, è, ñ, ü, ö, etc.), which is sufficient for `café` → `cafe` without the extra dependency; prefer the hand-rolled table unless the controller confirms `x/text` is already resolvable. `jsonjoinarray` parses `value` as JSON (`gjson.Parse`, args = `[path, sep]`) and joins the array at `path` with `sep`. `hexdump`/`strdump` log via `logging.FromContext(ctx).Debug("cardigann filter", "filter", name, "value", value)` and return `value` unchanged — debug-only, never transform. `validate`'s single arg is a comma-separated allow-list; return `value` unchanged if present (case-sensitive, matching the corpus's genre lists), else `""`.

- [ ] **Step 33: implement `Engine.Login`'s dispatch, `loginForm`, `loginCookie`**

The dispatcher and the form flow, precisely:
```go
func (e Engine) Login(ctx context.Context, def *Definition, cfg Config) (*Session, error) {
	lb := def.Login
	if lb == nil {
		return &Session{}, nil
	}
	if lb.Captcha != nil {
		if found, err := e.captchaPresent(ctx, def, cfg, lb); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		} else if found {
			return nil, &CaptchaRequiredError{Type: lb.Captcha.Type}
		}
	}
	switch lb.Method {
	case "", "form":
		return e.loginForm(ctx, def, cfg, lb)
	case "cookie":
		return e.loginCookie(ctx, def, cfg, lb)
	case "post":
		return e.loginPost(ctx, def, cfg, lb)
	case "get":
		return e.loginGet(ctx, def, cfg, lb)
	case "oneurl":
		return e.loginOneURL(ctx, def, cfg, lb)
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: unknown login method %q", lb.Method)
	}
}

func (e Engine) loginForm(ctx context.Context, def *Definition, cfg Config, lb *LoginBlock) (*Session, error) {
	tc := e.templateContext(def, cfg)
	page, err := e.get(ctx, cfg, lb.Path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	doc, err := ParseDoc(ResponseHTML, page)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: parse login page: %w", err)
	}

	form := url.Values{}
	for k, v := range lb.Inputs {
		rendered, err := render(string(v), tc)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		form.Set(k, rendered)
	}
	for name, sel := range lb.SelectorInputs {
		val, ok, err := sel.Extract(ctx, doc, tc)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if !ok && !sel.Optional {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: login selector input %q not found", name)
		}
		form.Set(name, val)
	}

	submitPath := lb.SubmitPath
	if submitPath == "" {
		submitPath = lb.Path
	}
	resp, respBody, err := e.postForm(ctx, cfg, submitPath, form)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := checkLoginErrors(ctx, respBody, lb.Error, tc); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &Session{Cookies: resp.Cookies(), ExpiresAt: time.Now().Add(30 * 24 * time.Hour)}, nil
}
```
`e.templateContext(def, cfg)` builds the shared `*TemplateContext` every one of `Login`/`Search`/`Download` renders against: `Config: cfg.Values`, `True: "true"`, `False: ""`, and `Now: now()` where `now := e.Now; if now == nil { now = time.Now }` — this is the one place `Engine.Now` is read, so every date-relative filter and `.Today.Year` a definition's templates use is deterministic under test whenever the caller sets `Engine.Now`. `Query`/`Keywords`/`Categories`/`Result` are populated by `Search` itself per-request, not here.

`loginCookie` reads each name in `lb.Cookies` out of `cfg.Values[name]` (a plain string setting, e.g. a `text` setting named to match — see the fixture's `session_id` setting-less-but-value-supplied pattern: `NewConfig`'s `raw` map is consulted directly for cookie names not declared in `def.Settings`, since `login.cookies` names arbitrary cookie names, not setting names) and builds `Session.Cookies` directly, erroring when a listed name has no value; runs `lb.Test` against the site (GET `lb.Test.Path`, assert `lb.Test.Selector` matches) when `Test != nil` — the two required tests above don't set `Test`, so this path only needs to exist, not be exercised yet (Step 35 adds `get`/`post`/`oneurl` plus the two signal errors and is a natural place to also cover `Test`). `loginPost` is `loginForm` minus the initial page GET and `SelectorInputs` scrape (POST `lb.Inputs` rendered, directly to `lb.Path`/`lb.SubmitPath`). `loginGet` is a GET to `lb.Path` with `lb.Inputs` as query parameters plus `lb.Headers`, checked against `lb.Error`. `loginOneURL` is `loginGet`'s request shape but treats the single fetched page as both the login action and its own test (no separate `Test` block is meaningful for a tracker whose "login" is one URL carrying the API key). `checkLoginErrors` parses the response body as HTML (login pages are always HTML per the corpus and schema) and, for each `ErrorBlock`, treats a matching `Selector` as failure — using `Message`'s rendered text (or a generic message) as `LoginError.Message`.

- [ ] **Step 38: implement `loginGet`/`loginPost`/`loginOneURL`, `captchaPresent`, and the shared HTTP helper's Cloudflare detection**

`captchaPresent` GETs `lb.Path` (or the site root when unset), parses HTML, and reports whether `lb.Captcha.Selector` matches. The engine's one shared low-level request function (`e.do`, used by every one of `get`/`postForm`/`fetch`) is where Cloudflare detection lives, so every code path (login, search, download) gets it for free:
```go
func (e Engine) do(ctx context.Context, req *http.Request) (*http.Response, []byte, error) {
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "cardigann."+req.Method)
	defer span.End()
	client := e.httpClient()
	resp, err := client.Do(req.WithContext(ctx))
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: request %s: %w", req.URL, err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: read response %s: %w", req.URL, err)
	}
	if (resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden || resp.StatusCode == http.StatusServiceUnavailable) &&
		looksLikeCloudflare(resp.Header) {
		err := &CloudflareChallengeError{StatusCode: resp.StatusCode}
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return resp, body, err
	}
	return resp, body, nil
}

func looksLikeCloudflare(h http.Header) bool {
	server := strings.ToLower(h.Get("Server"))
	return h.Get("cf-mitigated") != "" || strings.Contains(server, "cloudflare") || strings.Contains(server, "ddos-guard")
}
```
`e.httpClient()` returns `e.HTTP` when set else `http.DefaultClient`, wrapping its `Transport` with `e.Proxy` when non-nil (`&http.Client{Transport: e.Proxy, ...}` derived from the base client, not mutating a caller-owned `*http.Client`).

```go
import (

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/newznab"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/torznab"
)

// testClock is the fixed instant every Search/Download/Login test in this
// file passes as Engine.Now, so date-relative fixtures ("12:25am") assert
// an exact result instead of one that depends on the day the suite runs.
var testClock = time.Date(2026, 9, 18, 15, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

func TestEngineSearch1337xHTML(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Write(readTestdataBytes(t, "1337x-search.html"))
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	def, err := cardigann.Load(readTestdata(t, "1337x.yml"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	cfg, err := cardigann.NewConfig(def, srv.URL+"/", map[string]string{})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	eng := cardigann.Engine{HTTP: srv.Client(), Now: func() time.Time { return testClock }}
	rels, err := eng.Search(context.Background(), def, cfg, cardigann.Query{Type: "search", Q: "some movie"})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	// 1337x.yml declares four SearchPathBlock entries (movies/tv/music/other
	// pages) with no `categories:` restriction on any of them, so all four
	// always fire regardless of the query — this is what the real file does,
	// not a simplification (see Step 43's path-selection note). The fixture
	// server answers every request with the same 3-row table, so a correct
	// Engine.Search returns 4*3 = 12 raw rows; Engine never dedupes across
	// paths or indexers (that is indexarr's search worker's job, per note
	// §5's DeDupeReleases/infohash-then-guid rule), so 12 is the right
	// assertion here, not 3.
	require.Len(t, rels, 12)

	movie := findRelease(t, rels, "Some.Movie.2024.1080p.WEB-DL.DDP5.1.H.264-GRP")
	assert.Contains(t, movie.Categories, newznab.CatMoviesHD)
	size, err := cardigann.GetBytes("4.2 GB")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, size, movie.Size)
	require.NotNil(t, movie.Seeders)
	assert.EqualValues(t, 128, *movie.Seeders)
	assert.Equal(t, 2026, movie.PubDate.Year()) // 12:25am -> fuzzytime "today", relative to the fixed Engine.Now

	truncated := findRelease(t, rels, "Another.Show.S02E05.720p.HDTV.x264-GRP2") // title_optional wins: href-derived, not the "..." display text
	assert.Contains(t, truncated.Categories, newznab.CatTVHD)
	assert.Equal(t, time.September, truncated.PubDate.Month()) // "7am Sep. 14th" -> dateparse "htt MMM. d" (no year token -> year 0000, deliberately not asserted)

	old := findRelease(t, rels, "Old.Documentary.2019.DVDRip.x264-GRP3")
	assert.Contains(t, old.Categories, newznab.CatMoviesDVD)
	assert.Equal(t, 2011, old.PubDate.Year()) // "Apr. 18th '11" -> dateparse "MMM. d yy"
}

func findRelease(t *testing.T, rels []torznab.Release, title string) torznab.Release {
	t.Helper()
	for _, r := range rels {
		if r.Title == title {
			return r
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no release titled %q in %d results", title, len(rels))
```

Key pieces, in prose (full production code here would exceed this document's purpose — every function signature below is already fixed by **Produces**):
- `buildKeywords(q Query) string`: `q.Q`, plus `" S<season>E<episode>"` (zero-padded) appended when `q.Season`/`q.Ep` are set and `q.Q` doesn't already look like a full release title — table-tested with three cases (Q only; Q+season/ep; Q+year) as part of this step's test file.
- Path selection: iterate `def.Search.Paths` (or wrap `def.Search.Path` as a single implicit entry with no `Categories`); a path with an empty `Categories` always matches (1337x's own four paths declare no `categories:` field at all and therefore all four always fire — this is what the real file does, not a simplification); prefix `"!"` excludes. **Scoping decision, stated not hidden:** `inputs` merge as `merge(search.Inputs, path.Inputs)` (path wins) unconditionally; `path.InheritInputs` is decoded but not given distinct behaviour, since neither bundled fixture disambiguates its semantics from the always-merge default and the note's own description is underspecified — leave a one-line `// TODO(inheritinputs)` comment, do not guess further.
- Build each request: render `path.Path` as a template (`.Keywords`, `.Config.*`, `.Categories` all populated on the `TemplateContext` before rendering), GET with a query string or POST with a form body per `path.Method` (default GET); `$raw` input's rendered value is appended to the query/body verbatim (not `url.Values`-encoded) after every other input; empty-valued inputs are omitted unless `search.AllowEmptyInputs`.
- Parse the response per `path.Response.Type` (nil → `ResponseHTML`).
- Row iteration: `def.Search.Rows.Count` (if set) short-circuits to zero rows when it resolves to `"0"`/empty; `Rows.Selector` + `Rows.Attribute` (JSON: descend one more level, e.g. 0dayfiles' `attribute: attributes`) via `Doc.Rows`; `Rows.MissingAttributeEqualsNoResults` turns an attribute-descent miss into zero rows instead of an error; `Rows.After != 0 || Rows.DateHeaders != nil` returns `ErrUnsupportedRowFeature` for the whole search (both bundled fixtures have `After: 0` and `DateHeaders: nil`, so this never triggers on the required corpus).
- Field extraction per row: walk `def.Search.Fields` (`OrderedFields`, file order), call `entry.Block.Extract(ctx, row, tc)`, store into `tc.Result[entry.Name]` regardless of whether the name is canonical; **a canonical name with `ok == false` and no `Optional`/`Default` drops the row** (log at Debug, continue the outer loop, do not fail the whole `Search`) — this is note §3.8's rule verbatim. "Canonical" means an exact match against the schema's own field-name alternation (`download|magnet|infohash|details|comments|title|description|category|categorydesc|size|leechers|seeders|date|files|grabs|downloadvolumefactor|uploadvolumefactor|minimumratio|minimumseedtime|imdb|imdbid|tmdbid|rageid|tvdbid|tvmazeid|traktid|doubanid|poster|genre|year|author|booktitle|publisher|album|artist|label|track`, quoted directly from `schema-v11.json`'s `FieldsBlock` pattern) — an intermediate variable like `title_optional`/`date_year` only ever lands in `.Result`, never in the mapping step below. The `title|append`/`category|append`/`categorydesc|noappend` key forms are a second, separate **known gap**: decoding accepts them (they're valid `OrderedFields` entries, just with an unusual `Name`), but the mapping step treats any name containing `|` as non-canonical (falls into `.Result` only, same as an intermediate variable) rather than implementing the append semantics — neither bundled fixture uses this form.
- Map canonical `.Result` values onto `torznab.Release` per note §3.8: `title`→`Title`; `details`→`CommentURL`(absolutized against the chosen `def.Links[i]`/`cfg.BaseURL` with `net/url.Parse(base).ResolveReference`); `download`→`Link`, or leave `Link` empty and set `MagnetURL` when the value has a `"magnet:"` prefix; `magnet`→`MagnetURL` directly; `infohash`→`InfoHash`; `size`→`GetBytes`; `seeders`/`leechers`→`*int32` pointers, `Peers` = their sum when both present; `date`→`time.Parse(time.RFC3339, ...)` (every date-producing filter already normalizes to RFC3339 per Step 28); `category`/`categorydesc`→`Categories` via `CategoryMapper.FromTracker`/`FromTrackerDesc`; `grabs`/`files`→`*int32`; `downloadvolumefactor`/`uploadvolumefactor`→`*float64`, defaulting to `1.0` when the field is entirely absent from the definition (not merely empty for one row); `minimumratio`/`minimumseedtime`→`*float64`/`*int64`; `description`; `imdbid`/`imdb`→`IDs["imdb"]` (regex `tt\d+` or bare digits normalized to a 7-digit `tt%07d`); `tmdbid`/`tvdbid`/`rageid`/`tvmazeid`/`traktid`/`doubanid`→`IDs[...]` (plain strings; `tvmazeid` has no other name to collide with); `poster`→`Poster`; `genre`→`Attrs["genre"]` (split on `,`/`|`, since `torznab.Release` has no typed `Genres` field — confirmed against B6's actual struct, not the research note's older sketch which did have one); `year`/`author`/`booktitle`/`publisher`/`artist`/`album`/`label`/`track`→ the matching typed field where `torznab.Release` has one (`Group`? — it does not have `Author`/`BookTitle`/`Publisher`/`Artist`/`Album`/`Label`/`Track` as typed fields either; **cross-check finding, not this task's to resolve:** B6's `Release` struct has no music/book fields at all, unlike the research note's §11 sketch — put all of these into `Attrs[name] = []string{value}` instead, and flag this gap to the controller: either B6 needs music/book fields added, or catalogarr's future decision layer reads them out of `Attrs`). `GUID` = `details` (or `download` when `details` is absent) verbatim, unresolved — the one field the row's own URL supplies directly without a filter chain.

- [ ] **Step 48: implement the JSON response path (`ResponseBlock.Type == "json"`), the `$raw`/header/auth wiring, and the array-selector join rule**

Everything from Step 43 already covers the shared row/field machinery; this step is what's JSON-specific:
- `search.Headers` (rendered, e.g. `Authorization: ["Bearer {{ .Config.apikey }}"]`) are set on every request this `Search` call makes, search or login alike.
- `$raw` (0dayfiles: `"{{ range .Categories }}&categories[]={{.}}{{end}}"`) is rendered once and appended to the querystring verbatim, after every ordinary `key=value` pair.
- Empty-valued inputs (`seasonNumber`, `episodeNumber`, `imdbId`, `tmdbId`, `tvdbId` when the query doesn't set them) are dropped from the querystring entirely — `search.AllowEmptyInputs` is what would keep them, and it is unset in `0dayfiles-api.yml`.
- **Design decision worth documenting exactly where implemented:** a JSON selector matching an array with no further `.Attribute` descent (0dayfiles' `genre: {selector: meta.genres}`) joins the array's elements with `","` rather than returning gjson's raw JSON text (`["Action","Science Fiction"]`) — this is what makes the corpus's own `re_replace`/`jsonjoinarray`-free genre filter chain produce a sane plain-text result; the alternative (raw JSON text) would make every existing definition's genre filters silently operate on bracket-and-quote-laden garbage. This rule lives in `Doc.Text` (Step 23) already; this step's test is what proves it end-to-end against a real fixture.
- `_internal`/`_featured`/`double_upload`'s `case` maps rely on a verified goccy/go-yaml behaviour: bareword YAML keys `True:`/`False:` decode to the lower-case string keys `"true"`/`"false"` (confirmed with `go doc` + a scratch decode in this task's research pass), and JSON booleans stringify to the same lower-case `"true"`/`"false"` via `gjson.Result.String()` — so the case lookup needs no case-folding, a plain map hit is correct. Document this exact fact as a code comment at the `Case` lookup site; it is exactly the kind of thing a future reader will "fix" incorrectly (by adding `strings.ToLower`, which would be harmless here but wrong for genuinely case-sensitive case-maps like `freeleech`'s `"100%"`/`"0%"` keys) without the explanation.

- [ ] **Step 53: implement `Engine.Download`**

```go
func (e Engine) Download(ctx context.Context, def *Definition, cfg Config, link string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
	if strings.HasPrefix(link, "magnet:") {
		return io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(link)), nil
	}
	if def.Download == nil {
		return e.fetch(ctx, cfg, link)
	}
	db := def.Download
	tc := e.templateContext(def, cfg)

	var beforeDoc Doc
	if db.Before != nil {
		body, err := e.runBefore(ctx, def, cfg, db.Before)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		beforeDoc = body
	}

	page, err := e.fetch(ctx, cfg, link)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer page.Close()
	pageBytes, err := io.ReadAll(page)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: read download page: %w", err)
	}
	doc, err := ParseDoc(ResponseHTML, pageBytes)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	for _, sel := range db.Selectors {
		src := doc
		if sel.UseBeforeResponse {
			src = beforeDoc
		}
		renderedSelector, err := render(sel.Selector, tc)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		found, ok := src.Select(renderedSelector)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		val, ok := found.Text(sel.Attribute)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		for _, f := range sel.Filters {
			val, err = Filters[f.Name](ctx, val, f.Args, tc)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
		}
		return e.resolveLink(ctx, cfg, val)
	}

	if db.InfoHash != nil {
		return e.buildMagnet(ctx, def, cfg, db.InfoHash, beforeDoc, doc, tc)
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("cardigann: no download selector matched for %q", link)
}

func (e Engine) resolveLink(ctx context.Context, cfg Config, val string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
	if strings.HasPrefix(val, "magnet:") {
		return io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(val)), nil
	}
	return e.fetch(ctx, cfg, val)
}
```
`buildMagnet` extracts `Hash`/`Title` via their own `SelectorField` (same `Extract`-style logic as `SelectorBlock`, minus `Case`/`Default`/`Text` — `SelectorField` is the smaller schema type) and formats `"magnet:?xt=urn:btih:" + hash + "&dn=" + url.QueryEscape(title)` — no announce trackers, since `InfoHashBlock` carries none (a difference from the research note's parenthetical "hash+title+trackers"; the schema's actual `InfoHashBlock` only has `Hash`/`Title`/`UseBeforeResponse` — trust the schema over the note here, per the note-vs-spec precedence rule).

**Scope note (read before anything else):** the design spec's `pkg/subtitles` sketch (§7) bundles four concerns into one package: the missing-subtitle *planner* (`Plan`/`Wanted`, §2.2 of the research note), provider search/scoring/post-processing, and sidecar *naming* (`SidecarName`/`ParseSidecar`). This task's own Produces enumeration — Provider, Registry, Query/Candidate, Score/Weights, the typed errors, post-processing funcs, a Sidecar *writer* — deliberately excludes the planner and the naming/parsing functions. Reasons, both from the task's own reading list:
1. `pkg/naming` (Task B3) owns "sidecar subtitle naming" per the Phase B package table, and this task is told to *consume* an assumed `naming.SubtitlePath(mediaPath, lang, forced, hi string) (string, error)` rather than reproduce it — so path computation is not this package's job; it only writes bytes to an already-resolved path (see `Writer` below).
2. The missing-subtitle computation (`Wanted`) needs `Existing []ExistingSub` scanning (embedded probe rescan *and* sidecar directory scan) and profile-selector logic that is squarely `SubtitleRequest`/`SubtitleProfile` reconciliation — Phase F (`captionarr`), which is the only place allowed to import `api/subtitle`. Building it here would either import that CRD package (forbidden by this task's own instructions) or freeze a planner API this package cannot yet validate against the real controller loop.

Everything else spec §7 lists for `pkg/subtitles` — `LangKey`, `Query`, `Candidate`, `Provider`, `ProviderError`, `Score`, `MaxScore`, `PostProcess` — is built here per its literal signature. Where the signature needs a type spec did not spell out (`Existing`, the release-info shape inside `Query`), it is mirrored from the *real* `api/subtitle/v1alpha1` status field it corresponds to (read, never imported) or from the research note's Go design (§13), never invented from scratch.

**Interfaces — Produces:**

```go
package subtitles // import "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"

// --- lang.go ---

// LangKey is Bazarr's wanted-language identity — spec §7's exact type.
// "en", "en:forced" and "en:hi" are three distinct keys (research note
// §2.2, §13.1). Mirrors api/subtitle/v1alpha1.LanguageItem.Key's wire form
// (validated there by ^[A-Za-z]{2,8}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*(:forced)?(:hi)?$)
// without importing that package.
type LangKey string

// ParseLangKey splits a LangKey into its BCP-47 language tag and flags.
func ParseLangKey(k LangKey) (lang string, forced, hi bool, err error)

// FormatLangKey is ParseLangKey's inverse.
func FormatLangKey(lang string, forced, hi bool) LangKey

// --- types.go ---

// TargetRelease is the handful of pkg/release.ParsedRelease fields
// GuessMatches needs. B8 does not import pkg/release (a disjoint, parallel
// Phase B package) — the future search worker fills this in from the real
// parsed release of the local file being searched for.
type TargetRelease struct {
	Group, Source, Resolution, VideoCodec, AudioCodec, StreamingService, Edition string
}

// Query is spec §7's exact struct, with Release retyped to *TargetRelease
// (see above) instead of *release.ParsedRelease.
type Query struct {
	Kind      common.MediaKind
	Title     string
	Year      int
	IDs       map[string]string // "imdb", "tmdb", "parent_imdb", "parent_tmdb" — no "tt"/prefix, per OpenSubtitles
	Season, Episode int
	Hash      string // moviehash, 16 lowercase hex
	SizeBytes int64
	Release   *TargetRelease
	Languages []LangKey
}

// Candidate is spec §7's exact struct plus additive provider-search
// metadata (Uploader..FetchID) needed to implement Search/Download and
// Bazarr's trusted_sources/ai_translated filters — no spec-declared field
// is renamed or dropped.
type Candidate struct {
	Provider, ID, Language string
	HI, Forced             bool
	ReleaseInfo            string
	Matches                map[string]bool
	Score, ScoreWithoutHash int

	Uploader          string
	Trusted           bool
	AITranslated      bool
	MachineTranslated bool
	Downloads         int
	FetchID           string // provider-scoped fetch handle, e.g. OpenSubtitles file_id
}

// --- moviehash.go ---

var ErrFileTooSmallForHash = errors.New("subtitles: file smaller than 128 KiB, moviehash not computed")

// MovieHash implements the OpenSubtitles hash exactly (research note §4.4):
// filesize + Σ(first 64 KiB as little-endian uint64 words) +
// Σ(last 64 KiB as little-endian uint64 words), wrapping mod 2^64.
func MovieHash(f *os.File) (uint64, error)
func MovieHashString(h uint64) string // 16 lowercase hex digits

// --- score.go ---

const (
	MatchHash = "hash"; MatchSeries = "series"; MatchTitle = "title"; MatchYear = "year"
	MatchSeason = "season"; MatchEpisode = "episode"; MatchSource = "source"
	MatchReleaseGroup = "release_group"; MatchAudioCodec = "audio_codec"; MatchResolution = "resolution"
	MatchVideoCodec = "video_codec"; MatchHearingImpaired = "hearing_impaired"; MatchStreamingService = "streaming_service"
	MatchEdition = "edition"
)

const ( MaxEpisodeScore = 360; MaxMovieScore = 180 )

// MaxScore is spec §7's exact symbol.
var MaxScore = map[common.MediaKind]int{ common.MediaKindEpisode: MaxEpisodeScore, common.MediaKindMovie: MaxMovieScore }

// CandidateMatches resolves compute_score's hash-corroboration (research
// note §5 item 1) and hearing-impaired-bonus (item 2) steps into the final
// matches map Score sums. Not in spec's abbreviated §7 sketch — spec's
// Score signature is intentionally kept 2-arg-exact (see Score below); this
// function is the composable piece that makes that possible without losing
// the corroboration rule. isSpecial mirrors ParsedRelease.Special (season
// finales / specials skip the season+episode corroboration requirement).
func CandidateMatches(kind common.MediaKind, hashVerifiable, isSpecial bool, wantHI *bool, raw map[string]bool) map[string]bool

// Score is spec §7's exact signature: sums per-kind weights over an
// already-resolved matches map (research note §5 item 3).
func Score(kind common.MediaKind, matches map[string]bool) (score, without int)

// MinScore converts a profile's MinScorePercent into an absolute threshold:
// MaxScore[kind] * pct / 100 (integer math — no float, per CLAUDE.md).
func MinScore(kind common.MediaKind, pct int) int

// GuessMatches derives the Match keys a raw release_info string corroborates
// against target: release_group, source, resolution, video_codec,
// audio_codec, streaming_service, edition — case-insensitive token
// containment (research note §5 "guess_matches"), not full parsing; it does
// not import pkg/release.
func GuessMatches(target TargetRelease, releaseInfo string) map[string]bool

// --- provider.go ---

type Capabilities struct {
	Movies, Episodes bool
	ForcedSearch     bool // false for Bazarr's PROVIDERS_FORCED_OFF equivalents
	HashSearch       bool
	HashVerifiable   bool
	Languages        func(bcp47 string) bool
	NeedsSecrets     []string // "apiKey", "username", "password"
	Generates        bool     // true for a provider that fabricates rather than fetches (not shipped by B8)
}

// Provider is spec §7's Name/Search/Download/HIVerifiable plus Capabilities
// (this task's explicit ask). Download returns the served file name
// alongside the bytes — spec's literal 3-return signature
// ([]byte, string, error) — because OpenSubtitles' /download response
// carries file_name for format/extension sniffing before PostProcess runs.
type Provider interface {
	Name() string
	Capabilities() Capabilities
	Search(ctx context.Context, q Query) ([]Candidate, error)
	Download(ctx context.Context, c Candidate) (raw []byte, fileName string, err error)
	HIVerifiable() bool
}

// --- throttle.go ---

// ProviderError is spec §7's Kind/RetryAfter plus additive quota/identity
// fields the OpenSubtitles /download response and ThrottleFor both need.
type ProviderError struct {
	Provider   string
	Kind       string // one of the Kind* constants below — spec §7's exact 8-name comment, reconciled to Bazarr's real exception names (research note §10)
	RetryAfter time.Duration
	ResetAt    time.Time
	Remaining  int
	Err        error
}
func (e *ProviderError) Error() string
func (e *ProviderError) Unwrap() error

const (
	KindTooManyRequests    = "TooManyRequests"
	KindDownloadLimitExceeded = "DownloadLimitExceeded"
	KindServiceUnavailable = "ServiceUnavailable"
	KindAPIThrottled       = "APIThrottled"
	KindParse              = "Parse"
	KindTimeout            = "Timeout"
	KindAuth               = "Auth"
	KindConfig             = "Config"
)

func IsQuotaExceeded(err error) bool // Kind == KindDownloadLimitExceeded
func IsRateLimited(err error) bool   // Kind == KindTooManyRequests

// ThrottleFor is spec §7's exact signature: the verbatim duration table
// (spec §6.5, research note §10), with a provider-supplied RetryAfter
// (Retry-After header, OpenSubtitles reset_time, Gestdown's 423 30 s hint)
// taking precedence over the static table when present.
func ThrottleFor(provider string, err error) (reason string, d time.Duration)

// --- registry.go ---

var ErrDuplicateProvider = errors.New("subtitles: provider already registered")

type Registry struct{ /* unexported */ }
func NewRegistry() *Registry
func (r *Registry) Register(p Provider) error // ErrDuplicateProvider on repeat Name()
func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (Provider, bool)
func (r *Registry) All() []Provider // registration order
func (r *Registry) For(kind common.MediaKind) []Provider // filters by Capabilities().Movies/Episodes

// --- himods.go, postprocess.go ---

// Mod* mirror api/subtitle/v1alpha1.SubtitleMod's exact enum values
// (removeHI;removeTags;ocrFixes;common;fixUppercase;reverseRTL;color) —
// mirrored, not imported.
const (
	ModRemoveHI = "removeHI"; ModRemoveTags = "removeTags"; ModOCRFixes = "ocrFixes"; ModCommon = "common"
	ModFixUppercase = "fixUppercase"; ModReverseRTL = "reverseRTL"; ModColor = "color"
)

// PostProcess is spec §7's exact signature: decode to UTF-8, convert to SRT
// unless !toSRT (profile.originalFormat), apply mods in order, always
// return valid UTF-8 SRT (or the original format's UTF-8 bytes).
func PostProcess(raw []byte, lang string, mods []string, toSRT bool) ([]byte, error)

// FixMojibake repairs the single most common, mechanically reversible
// mojibake case: UTF-8 bytes that were mis-decoded and re-saved as
// Windows-1252/Latin-1 (e.g. "café" -> "cafÃ©"). This is deliberately
// narrower than ftfy (research note §6.2: "no Go equivalent... skip"); it
// covers the one pattern that is safely detectable without a statistical
// model.
func FixMojibake(s string) string

// --- sidecar.go ---

// Writer writes already-normalised subtitle content to an already-resolved
// path atomically (temp file + rename same-directory). It does not compute
// the path itself — see the naming.SubtitlePath note under Consumes.
type Writer struct{}
func NewWriter() Writer
func (Writer) Write(ctx context.Context, path string, content []byte) error
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `lang.go`**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

type LangKey string

func ParseLangKey(k LangKey) (lang string, forced, hi bool, err error) {
	s := string(k)
	if s == "" {
		return "", false, false, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: empty langKey")
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ":")
	switch len(parts) {
	case 1:
		return parts[0], false, false, nil
	case 2:
		switch parts[1] {
		case "forced":
			return parts[0], true, false, nil
		case "hi":
			return parts[0], false, true, nil
		default:
			return "", false, false, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: langKey %q: unknown suffix %q", s, parts[1])
		}
	default:
		return "", false, false, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: langKey %q: forced and hi are mutually exclusive", s)
	}
}

func FormatLangKey(lang string, forced, hi bool) LangKey {
	switch {
	case forced:
		return LangKey(lang + ":forced")
	case hi:
		return LangKey(lang + ":hi")
	default:
		return LangKey(lang)
	}
}
```

```go
package subtitles_test

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"

func TestMovieHashZeroFilledFileEqualsItsSize(t *testing.T) {
	// A zero-filled file is endianness-independent (every summed word is 0),
	// so this only proves size accounting and the two-chunk read are right.
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "zero.bin")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, make([]byte, 300000), 0o644))

	f, err := os.Open(path)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer f.Close()

	h, err := subtitles.MovieHash(f)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, uint64(300000), h)
	assert.Equal(t, "00000000000493e0", subtitles.MovieHashString(h))
}

func TestMovieHashPatternedFileMatchesAPinnedVector(t *testing.T) {
	// buf[i] = byte(i % 256) over 200000 bytes. The first 64 KiB starts at
	// pattern-phase 0; the last 64 KiB starts at offset 200000-65536=134464,
	// pattern-phase 134464%256=64 — a genuinely different, order-dependent
	// chunk, so this exercises the little-endian summation for real (unlike
	// the zero-fill case above). Value below was computed once by running
	// this exact algorithm against this exact byte sequence.
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "pattern.bin")
	buf := make([]byte, 200000)
	for i := range buf {
		buf[i] = byte(i % 256)
	}
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, buf, 0o644))

	f, err := os.Open(path)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer f.Close()

	h, err := subtitles.MovieHash(f)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "a0601fdf9f620d40", subtitles.MovieHashString(h))
}

func TestMovieHashRejectsFilesUnder128KiB(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "small.bin")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, make([]byte, 131071), 0o644)) // one byte short of 2*64KiB

	f, err := os.Open(path)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer f.Close()

	_, err = subtitles.MovieHash(f)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, subtitles.ErrFileTooSmallForHash)
}
```

- [x] **Step 6: Implement `moviehash.go` — REMOVED by controller amendment 3; skip.**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
)

const movieHashChunk = 64 * 1024

var ErrFileTooSmallForHash = errors.New("subtitles: file smaller than 128 KiB, moviehash not computed")

// MovieHash implements the OpenSubtitles hash exactly (research note §4.4):
// filesize + sum(first 64KiB as little-endian uint64 words) +
// sum(last 64KiB as little-endian uint64 words), wrapping mod 2^64.
func MovieHash(f *os.File) (uint64, error) {
	st, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: stat: %w", err)
	}
	if st.Size() < 2*movieHashChunk {
		return 0, ErrFileTooSmallForHash
	}
	sum := uint64(st.Size())
	buf := make([]byte, movieHashChunk)
	for _, off := range []int64{0, st.Size() - movieHashChunk} {
		if _, err := f.ReadAt(buf, off); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: read at %d: %w", off, err)
		}
		for i := 0; i < movieHashChunk; i += 8 {
			sum += binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[i:])
		}
	}
	return sum, nil
}

func MovieHashString(h uint64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%016x", h) }
```

```go
package subtitles

import common "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"

const (
	MatchHash = "hash"; MatchSeries = "series"; MatchTitle = "title"; MatchYear = "year"
	MatchSeason = "season"; MatchEpisode = "episode"; MatchSource = "source"
	MatchReleaseGroup = "release_group"; MatchAudioCodec = "audio_codec"; MatchResolution = "resolution"
	MatchVideoCodec = "video_codec"; MatchHearingImpaired = "hearing_impaired"; MatchStreamingService = "streaming_service"
	MatchEdition = "edition"
)

const ( MaxEpisodeScore = 360; MaxMovieScore = 180 )

var MaxScore = map[common.MediaKind]int{ common.MediaKindEpisode: MaxEpisodeScore, common.MediaKindMovie: MaxMovieScore }

// episodeWeights/movieWeights are research note §5's DEFAULT_SCORES table, verbatim.
var episodeWeights = map[string]int{
	MatchHash: 359, MatchSeries: 160, MatchYear: 90, MatchSeason: 30, MatchEpisode: 30,
	MatchSource: 25, MatchReleaseGroup: 20, MatchAudioCodec: 1, MatchResolution: 1,
	MatchVideoCodec: 1, MatchHearingImpaired: 1, MatchStreamingService: 1,
}
var movieWeights = map[string]int{
	MatchHash: 179, MatchTitle: 60, MatchYear: 40, MatchSource: 30, MatchEdition: 30,
	MatchReleaseGroup: 15, MatchAudioCodec: 1, MatchResolution: 1, MatchVideoCodec: 1,
	MatchHearingImpaired: 1, MatchStreamingService: 1,
}

func weightsFor(kind common.MediaKind) map[string]int {
	if kind == common.MediaKindMovie {
		return movieWeights
	}
	return episodeWeights // episode is the only other subtitle-eligible kind (design spec §4.6)
}

// Score is spec §7's exact signature.
func Score(kind common.MediaKind, matches map[string]bool) (score, without int) {
	w := weightsFor(kind)
	for m, ok := range matches {
		if ok {
			score += w[m]
		}
	}
	without = score
	if matches[MatchHash] {
		without = score - w[MatchHash]
	}
	return score, without
}

// MinScore converts a percentage threshold into an absolute score.
func MinScore(kind common.MediaKind, pct int) int {
	return MaxScore[kind] * pct / 100
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Implement `CandidateMatches`**

Append to `score.go`:
```go
// CandidateMatches implements compute_score's hash-corroboration and
// hearing-impaired-bonus steps (research note §5 items 1-2). wantHI is the
// candidate's own HI flag compared against the profile's HI preference for
// this language; nil means no preference is set (Bazarr's "prefer": either
// is fine, no bonus either way).
func CandidateMatches(kind common.MediaKind, hashVerifiable, isSpecial bool, wantHIMatch *bool, raw map[string]bool) map[string]bool {
	out := make(map[string]bool, len(raw))
	for k, v := range raw {
		out[k] = v
	}

	if out[MatchHash] {
		corroborated := !hashVerifiable // an unverifiable provider is trusted outright
		if hashVerifiable {
			if kind == common.MediaKindMovie {
				corroborated = out[MatchVideoCodec] && out[MatchSource]
			} else {
				corroborated = out[MatchSeries] && out[MatchSource] && (isSpecial || (out[MatchSeason] && out[MatchEpisode]))
			}
		}
		if corroborated {
			out = map[string]bool{MatchHash: true}
		} else {
			delete(out, MatchHash)
		}
	}

	if wantHIMatch != nil && *wantHIMatch {
		out[MatchHearingImpaired] = true
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
// GuessMatches derives Match keys a raw release_info string corroborates
// against target via case-insensitive token containment. It never imports
// pkg/release; full release parsing is that package's job.
func GuessMatches(target TargetRelease, releaseInfo string) map[string]bool {
	lower := strings.ToLower(releaseInfo)
	out := map[string]bool{}
	for field, key := range map[string]string{
		target.Group: MatchReleaseGroup, target.Source: MatchSource, target.Resolution: MatchResolution,
		target.VideoCodec: MatchVideoCodec, target.AudioCodec: MatchAudioCodec,
		target.StreamingService: MatchStreamingService, target.Edition: MatchEdition,
	} {
		if field != "" && strings.Contains(lower, strings.ToLower(field)) {
			out[key] = true
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"errors"
	"sync"

	common "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
)

var ErrDuplicateProvider = errors.New("subtitles: provider already registered")

type Registry struct {
	mu    sync.RWMutex
	byName map[string]Provider
	order  []string
}

func NewRegistry() *Registry { return &Registry{byName: map[string]Provider{}} }

func (r *Registry) Register(p Provider) error {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if _, exists := r.byName[p.Name()]; exists {
		return ErrDuplicateProvider
	}
	r.byName[p.Name()] = p
	r.order = append(r.order, p.Name())
	return nil
}

func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (Provider, bool) {
	r.mu.RLock()
	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
	p, ok := r.byName[name]
	return p, ok
}

func (r *Registry) All() []Provider {
	r.mu.RLock()
	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
	out := make([]Provider, 0, len(r.order))
	for _, name := range r.order {
		out = append(out, r.byName[name])
	}
	return out
}

func (r *Registry) For(kind common.MediaKind) []Provider {
	var out []Provider
	for _, p := range r.All() {
		c := p.Capabilities()
		if (kind == common.MediaKindMovie && c.Movies) || (kind == common.MediaKindEpisode && c.Episodes) {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
	Languages        func(bcp47 string) bool
	NeedsSecrets     []string
	Generates        bool
}

// Provider is spec §7's Name/Search/Download/HIVerifiable plus Capabilities.
type Provider interface {
	Name() string
	Capabilities() Capabilities
	Search(ctx context.Context, q Query) ([]Candidate, error)
	Download(ctx context.Context, c Candidate) (raw []byte, fileName string, err error)
	HIVerifiable() bool
}
```

- [ ] **Step 18: Implement `throttle.go`**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

type ProviderError struct {
	Provider   string
	Kind       string
	RetryAfter time.Duration
	ResetAt    time.Time
	Remaining  int
	Err        error
}

func (e *ProviderError) Error() string {
	if e.Err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprintf("subtitles: %s: %s: %v", e.Provider, e.Kind, e.Err)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("subtitles: %s: %s", e.Provider, e.Kind)
}
func (e *ProviderError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }

const (
	KindTooManyRequests       = "TooManyRequests"
	KindDownloadLimitExceeded = "DownloadLimitExceeded"
	KindServiceUnavailable    = "ServiceUnavailable"
	KindAPIThrottled          = "APIThrottled"
	KindParse                 = "Parse"
	KindTimeout               = "Timeout"
	KindAuth                  = "Auth"
	KindConfig                = "Config"
)

func kindOf(err error) (string, bool) {
	var pe *ProviderError
	if errors.As(err, &pe) {
		return pe.Kind, true
	}
	return "", false
}

func IsQuotaExceeded(err error) bool { k, ok := kindOf(err); return ok && k == KindDownloadLimitExceeded }
func IsRateLimited(err error) bool   { k, ok := kindOf(err); return ok && k == KindTooManyRequests }

// defaultDurations is spec §6.5 / research note §10's verbatim table.
var defaultDurations = map[string]time.Duration{
	KindTooManyRequests: time.Hour, KindDownloadLimitExceeded: 3 * time.Hour,
	KindServiceUnavailable: 20 * time.Minute, KindAPIThrottled: 10 * time.Minute,
	KindParse: 6 * time.Hour, KindTimeout: time.Hour, KindAuth: 12 * time.Hour, KindConfig: 12 * time.Hour,
}

// providerOverrides is research note §10's per-provider column.
var providerOverrides = map[string]map[string]time.Duration{
	"opensubtitlescom": {KindTooManyRequests: time.Minute, KindDownloadLimitExceeded: 6 * time.Hour},
}

// ThrottleFor is spec §7's exact signature.
func ThrottleFor(provider string, err error) (reason string, d time.Duration) {
	var pe *ProviderError
	if !errors.As(err, &pe) {
		return "unknown", time.Hour
	}
	if pe.RetryAfter > 0 {
		return pe.Kind, pe.RetryAfter
	}
	if byProvider, ok := providerOverrides[provider]; ok {
		if d, ok := byProvider[pe.Kind]; ok {
			return pe.Kind, d
		}
	}
	return pe.Kind, defaultDurations[pe.Kind]
}
```

- [ ] **Step 21: Implement `himods.go`**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/dlclark/regexp2"
)

// soundCueKeywords gates HI_all_caps (research note §6.3): an all-caps line
// is only a hearing-impaired cue, not shouted dialogue, when it names a
// sound.
var soundCueKeywords = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)LAUGH|APPLAU|CHEER|MUSIC|GASP|SIGH|GROAN|COUGH|SCREAM|SHOUT|WHISPER|PHONE|DOOR|KNOCK|FOOTSTEP|THUNDER|EXPLOSION|GUNSHOT|SIREN`)

// hiBrackets matches a bracketed sound cue anywhere in the line, e.g.
// "I heard [a noise] outside." -> "I heard  outside." (regexp2 port of
// Bazarr's HI_brackets, research note §6.3; TAG's optional-style-tag
// wrapper is dropped — this package's inputs are already-decoded plain
// text by the time mods run).
var hiBrackets = mustHI(`-?["']*\[(?=[^\[\]]{3,})[A-Za-zÀ-ž0-9\s'".:_&+-]+[)\]]["']*[\s:]*`, regexp2.None)

// hiBracketsFull matches a line that is *entirely* a bracketed cue.
var hiBracketsFull = mustHI(`^-?[([].+[)\]]$`, regexp2.Singleline)

// hiSpeakerLabel matches an upper-case "NAME:" label at the start of a line
// (a simplified, RE2-portable core of Bazarr's HI_before_colon_caps).
var hiSpeakerLabel = mustHI(`^[A-ZÀ-Ž][A-ZÀ-Ž0-9 '&+-]{1,30}:\s*`, regexp2.None)

func mustHI(pattern string, opts regexp2.RegexOptions) *regexp2.Regexp {
	re := regexp2.MustCompile(pattern, opts)
	re.MatchTimeout = 2 * time.Second // CLAUDE.md: always set a MatchTimeout on regexp2
	return re
}

func replaceAll(re *regexp2.Regexp, s, repl string) (string, error) {
	return re.Replace(s, repl, -1, -1)
}

// RemoveHI ports Bazarr's hearing-impaired stripping (research note §6.3)
// line by line. It implements the bracket, speaker-label and gated
// all-caps rules; the remaining patterns from the same note section
// (before-colon-noncaps, starting-upper-then-sentence, JP_parentheses,
// music symbols) port the same way — same mustHI/replaceAll mechanism,
// added as new package-level *regexp2.Regexp values plus a case in the
// loop below.
func RemoveHI(text string) (string, error) {
	lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
	out := make([]string, 0, len(lines))
	for _, line := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if trimmed == "" {
			continue
		}
		if m, err := hiBracketsFull.MatchString(trimmed); err != nil {
			return "", err
		} else if m {
			continue // whole line was a bracketed cue
		}
		if isAllCapsSoundCue(trimmed) {
			continue
		}
		line, err := replaceAll(hiBrackets, line, "")
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		line, err = replaceAll(hiSpeakerLabel, line, "")
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		out = append(out, line)
	}
	return strings.Join(out, "\n"), nil
}

func isAllCapsSoundCue(line string) bool {
	if line != strings.ToUpper(line) {
		return false
	}
	hasLetter := false
	for _, r := range line {
		if (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= 'À' && r <= 'Ž') {
			hasLetter = true
			break
		}
	}
	return hasLetter && soundCueKeywords.MatchString(line)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 24: Implement `FixMojibake` and the charset half of `postprocess.go`**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"golang.org/x/text/encoding"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/charmap"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/japanese"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/korean"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/simplifiedchinese"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/traditionalchinese"
	"golang.org/x/text/encoding/unicode"
)

// languageEncodings is research note §6.1's per-language candidate table,
// abbreviated to the language families this package's provider set (OS.com,
// Gestdown, embedded) actually returns most: CJK, Cyrillic, Central
// European, Western European. Each candidate is tried in order; the first
// one that both decodes without error and round-trips to valid UTF-8 wins.
var languageEncodings = map[string][]encoding.Encoding{
	"zh": {simplifiedchinese.GBK, traditionalchinese.Big5},
	"ja": {japanese.ShiftJIS, japanese.EUCJP},
	"ko": {korean.EUCKR},
	"ru": {charmap.Windows1251, charmap.ISO8859_5},
	"bg": {charmap.Windows1251, charmap.ISO8859_5},
	"uk": {charmap.Windows1251, charmap.ISO8859_5},
	"pl": {charmap.Windows1250, charmap.ISO8859_2},
	"cs": {charmap.Windows1250, charmap.ISO8859_2},
	"el": {charmap.Windows1253, charmap.ISO8859_7},
	"tr": {charmap.Windows1254, charmap.ISO8859_9},
}

// defaultEncodings is Bazarr's Western-default candidate chain.
var defaultEncodings = []encoding.Encoding{charmap.Windows1252, charmap.ISO8859_1}

// decodeToUTF8 sniffs a BOM, accepts already-valid UTF-8 as-is, and
// otherwise tries the language's candidate encodings (falling back to the
// Western default chain), returning the first clean decode.
func decodeToUTF8(raw []byte, lang string) ([]byte, error) {
	if bytes.HasPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF}) {
		return raw[3:], nil
	}
	if bom, err := unicode.UTF16(unicode.LittleEndian, unicode.ExpectBOM).NewDecoder().Bytes(raw); err == nil && bytes.HasPrefix(raw, []byte{0xFF, 0xFE}) {
		return bom, nil
	}
	if bom, err := unicode.UTF16(unicode.BigEndian, unicode.ExpectBOM).NewDecoder().Bytes(raw); err == nil && bytes.HasPrefix(raw, []byte{0xFE, 0xFF}) {
		return bom, nil
	}
	if utf8.Valid(raw) {
		return raw, nil
	}

	candidates := append(append([]encoding.Encoding{}, languageEncodings[baseLang(lang)]...), defaultEncodings...)
	for _, enc := range candidates {
		if out, err := enc.NewDecoder().Bytes(raw); err == nil && utf8.Valid(out) {
			return out, nil
		}
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: could not decode subtitle to UTF-8 (lang=%s)", lang)
}

func baseLang(lang string) string {
	if i := bytes.IndexByte([]byte(lang), '-'); i >= 0 {
		return lang[:i]
	}
	return lang
}

// FixMojibake repairs UTF-8 bytes that were mis-decoded and re-saved as
// Windows-1252/Latin-1 — the one mojibake pattern that is mechanically
// reversible without a statistical model (research note §6.2 found no Go
// equivalent to ftfy; this covers the single highest-value case instead of
// skipping the requirement outright). Detection: re-encoding s as
// Windows-1252 and decoding the result as UTF-8 succeeds and changes
// nothing structurally wrong — i.e. s itself is valid UTF-8 that decodes
// from a Windows-1252 byte sequence which is *also* valid UTF-8 containing
// the CP1252 tell-tale bytes (0xC3 followed by a Latin-1 continuation).
func FixMojibake(s string) string {
	cp1252 := charmap.Windows1252
	reencoded, err := cp1252.NewEncoder().String(s)
	if err != nil {
		return s // s contains characters outside Windows-1252 — not this pattern
	}
	if !utf8.ValidString(reencoded) {
		return s
	}
	if reencoded == s {
		return s // nothing changed — not mojibake
	}
	// Only accept the repair if it strictly reduces non-ASCII byte noise
	// (Ã, Â, â€” and friends) — never applied to already-clean text.
	if !bytes.ContainsAny([]byte(s), "ÃÂ") {
		return s
	}
	return reencoded
}
```

- [ ] **Step 26: Implement `PostProcess` (the composition) and the format-conversion half of `postprocess.go`**

```go
// (append to postprocess.go)

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/asticode/go-astisub"
)

// PostProcess is spec §7's exact signature: decode to UTF-8, convert to SRT
// unless !toSRT, apply mods in mods order, always return valid UTF-8.
func PostProcess(raw []byte, lang string, mods []string, toSRT bool) ([]byte, error) {
	decoded, err := decodeToUTF8(raw, lang)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	body := decoded
	if toSRT {
		body, err = convertToSRT(decoded)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	text := string(body)
	for _, mod := range mods {
		switch mod {
		case ModRemoveHI:
			text, err = RemoveHI(text)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: removeHI: %w", err)
			}
		case ModCommon:
			text = FixMojibake(text)
		case ModFixUppercase:
			text = fixUppercase(text)
		case ModRemoveTags, ModOCRFixes, ModReverseRTL, ModColor:
			// Deferred: no fixture-verified behaviour for these yet. Recognised
			// (not an error) so a profile listing them does not fail PostProcess;
			// add a real implementation + test the same way as ModRemoveHI once
			// one is needed by the captionarr worker.
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: unknown mod %q", mod)
		}
	}
	return []byte(text), nil
}

// convertToSRT sniffs ASS/SSA by content ("[Script Info]" section header,
// research note §6 item 4) and converts via go-astisub; anything else is
// assumed to already be SRT and is returned unchanged.
func convertToSRT(raw []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if !bytes.Contains(raw, []byte("[Script Info]")) {
		return raw, nil
	}
	subs, err := astisub.ReadFromSSA(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: parse ASS/SSA: %w", err)
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	if err := subs.WriteToSRT(&buf); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: write SRT: %w", err)
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

func fixUppercase(s string) string { return s } // TODO(next): port Bazarr's fix_uppercase heuristic when a fixture needs it
```

- [ ] **Step 29: Implement `sidecar.go`**

```go
package subtitles

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

// Writer writes already-normalised subtitle content to an already-resolved
// path atomically. It does not compute the destination path — see the
// naming.SubtitlePath note in this task's Consumes section.
type Writer struct{}

func NewWriter() Writer { return Writer{} }

func (Writer) Write(ctx context.Context, path string, content []byte) error {
	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".subtitles-*.tmp")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: create temp file in %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	tmpName := tmp.Name()
	defer os.Remove(tmpName) // no-op once the rename below succeeds

	if _, err := tmp.Write(content); err != nil {
		tmp.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: write %s: %w", tmpName, err)
	}
	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: close %s: %w", tmpName, err)
	}
	if err := os.Rename(tmpName, path); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: rename %s to %s: %w", tmpName, path, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

- [ ] **Step 32: Implement `client.go` (config, rate limiter, login/token cache, HTTP plumbing)**

```go
package opensubtitlescom

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/time/rate"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/logging"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/tracing"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

const defaultEndpoint = "https://api.opensubtitles.com/api/v1"

type Config struct {
	APIKey, Username, Password, UserAgent string
	Endpoint   string
	HTTPClient *http.Client
	Limiter    *rate.Limiter
}

type Provider struct {
	cfg Config

	mu        sync.Mutex
	token     string
	baseURL   string
	tokenAt   time.Time
}

func New(cfg Config) *Provider {
	if cfg.Endpoint == "" {
		cfg.Endpoint = defaultEndpoint
	}
	if cfg.HTTPClient == nil {
		cfg.HTTPClient = http.DefaultClient
	}
	if cfg.Limiter == nil {
		cfg.Limiter = rate.NewLimiter(5, 5) // 5 req/s per IP, research note §4.3
	}
	return &Provider{cfg: cfg, baseURL: cfg.Endpoint}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string { return "opensubtitlescom" }
func (p *Provider) HIVerifiable() bool { return true }
func (p *Provider) Capabilities() subtitles.Capabilities {
	return subtitles.Capabilities{
		Movies: true, Episodes: true, ForcedSearch: true, HashSearch: true, HashVerifiable: true,
		NeedsSecrets: []string{"apiKey", "username", "password"},
	}
}

type loginResponse struct {
	Token   string `json:"token"`
	BaseURL string `json:"base_url"`
	User    struct {
		VIP bool `json:"vip"`
	} `json:"user"`
}

// EnsureLoggedIn logs in if there is no cached token, or the cached one is
// older than 12h (Bazarr's TOKEN_EXPIRATION_TIME, half the real 24h JWT
// life — research note §4.3).
func (p *Provider) EnsureLoggedIn(ctx context.Context) error {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if p.token != "" && time.Since(p.tokenAt) < 12*time.Hour {
		return nil
	}

	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.opensubtitlescom.login")
	defer span.End()

	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"username": p.cfg.Username, "password": p.cfg.Password})
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, p.cfg.Endpoint+"/login", bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	p.setCommonHeaders(req)

	if err := p.cfg.Limiter.Wait(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	resp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom login: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		err := statusToProviderError(p.Name(), resp)
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return err
	}

	var lr loginResponse
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&lr); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom login: decode: %w", err)
	}
	p.token = lr.Token
	p.tokenAt = time.Now()
	if lr.BaseURL != "" {
		p.baseURL = "https://" + lr.BaseURL + "/api/v1"
		if p.cfg.Endpoint != defaultEndpoint {
			p.baseURL = p.cfg.Endpoint // test/mirror endpoints keep their own base
		}
	}
	logging.FromContext(ctx).Debug("opensubtitlescom login ok", "vip", lr.User.VIP)
	return nil
}

func (p *Provider) setCommonHeaders(req *http.Request) {
	req.Header.Set("Api-Key", p.cfg.APIKey)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	ua := p.cfg.UserAgent
	if ua == "" {
		ua = "clustarr v0"
	}
	req.Header.Set("User-Agent", ua)
	p.mu.Lock()
	tok := p.token
	p.mu.Unlock()
	if tok != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+tok)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 34: Implement `Search` in `provider.go`**

Create `pkg/subtitles/providers/opensubtitlescom/provider.go`:
```go
package opensubtitlescom

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/tracing"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

type searchResponse struct {
	Data []struct {
		Attributes struct {
			Language          string  `json:"language"`
			HearingImpaired   bool    `json:"hearing_impaired"`
			ForeignPartsOnly  bool    `json:"foreign_parts_only"`
			FromTrusted       bool    `json:"from_trusted"`
			AITranslated      bool    `json:"ai_translated"`
			MachineTranslated bool    `json:"machine_translated"`
			DownloadCount     int     `json:"download_count"`
			Release           string  `json:"release"`
			MoviehashMatch    bool    `json:"moviehash_match"`
			Uploader          struct{ Name string `json:"name"` } `json:"uploader"`
			Files             []struct {
				FileID int    `json:"file_id"`
				FileName string `json:"file_name"`
			} `json:"files"`
		} `json:"attributes"`
	} `json:"data"`
}

func (p *Provider) Search(ctx context.Context, q subtitles.Query) ([]subtitles.Candidate, error) {
	if err := p.EnsureLoggedIn(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.opensubtitlescom.search")
	defer span.End()

	params := url.Values{}
	if v, ok := q.IDs["imdb"]; ok {
		params.Set("imdb_id", v)
	}
	if v, ok := q.IDs["tmdb"]; ok {
		params.Set("tmdb_id", v)
	}
	if q.Hash != "" {
		params.Set("moviehash", q.Hash)
	}
	if q.Season > 0 {
		params.Set("season_number", strconv.Itoa(q.Season))
	}
	if q.Episode > 0 {
		params.Set("episode_number", strconv.Itoa(q.Episode))
	}
	params.Set("type", osType(q.Kind))
	params.Set("ai_translated", "exclude")

	langs := make([]string, 0, len(q.Languages))
	hi, forced := "include", "exclude"
	for _, lk := range q.Languages {
		lang, isForced, isHI, err := subtitles.ParseLangKey(lk)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		langs = append(langs, strings.ToLower(lang))
		switch {
		case isForced:
			hi, forced = "exclude", "only"
		case isHI:
			hi, forced = "only", "exclude"
		}
	}
	params.Set("languages", strings.Join(langs, ","))
	params.Set("hearing_impaired", hi)
	params.Set("foreign_parts_only", forced)

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, p.baseURL+"/subtitles?"+params.Encode(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	p.setCommonHeaders(req)

	if err := p.cfg.Limiter.Wait(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	resp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom search: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		err := statusToProviderError(p.Name(), resp)
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, err
	}

	var sr searchResponse
	if err := jsonDecode(resp, &sr); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	out := make([]subtitles.Candidate, 0, len(sr.Data))
	for _, d := range sr.Data {
		a := d.Attributes
		if len(a.Files) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		matches := map[string]bool{}
		if a.MoviehashMatch {
			matches[subtitles.MatchHash] = true
		}
		out = append(out, subtitles.Candidate{
			Provider: p.Name(), FetchID: strconv.Itoa(a.Files[0].FileID),
			Language: a.Language, HI: a.HearingImpaired, Forced: a.ForeignPartsOnly && !a.HearingImpaired,
			ReleaseInfo: a.Release, Matches: matches,
			Uploader: a.Uploader.Name, Trusted: a.FromTrusted,
			AITranslated: a.AITranslated, MachineTranslated: a.MachineTranslated, Downloads: a.DownloadCount,
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func osType(kind interface{ String() string }) string { return "" } // replaced below
```

```go
func TestDownloadFetchesTheLinkedFileAndReturnsItsName(t *testing.T) {
	const srtBody = "1\n00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,000\nHello.\n"
	srv := newTestServer(t, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
```

```go
type downloadResponse struct {
	Link     string `json:"link"`
	FileName string `json:"file_name"`
}

func (p *Provider) Download(ctx context.Context, c subtitles.Candidate) ([]byte, string, error) {
	if err := p.EnsureLoggedIn(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.opensubtitlescom.download")
	defer span.End()

	fileID, err := strconv.Atoi(c.FetchID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom: invalid FetchID %q: %w", c.FetchID, err)
	}
	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"file_id": fileID, "sub_format": "srt"})
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, p.baseURL+"/download", bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	p.setCommonHeaders(req)

	if err := p.cfg.Limiter.Wait(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	resp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom download: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		err := statusToProviderError(p.Name(), resp)
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, "", err
	}

	var dr downloadResponse
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&dr); err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom download: decode: %w", err)
	}

	fileReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, dr.Link, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	fileResp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(fileReq)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom fetch link: %w", err)
	}
	defer fileResp.Body.Close()
	raw, err := io.ReadAll(fileResp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: opensubtitlescom read body: %w", err)
	}
	return raw, dr.FileName, nil
}
```

- [ ] **Step 39: Implement `statusToProviderError`**

Create the remainder of `client.go`'s error mapping (append):
```go
import (
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

// statusToProviderError maps an OpenSubtitles HTTP response to
// subtitles.ProviderError per research note §4.3's status table.
func statusToProviderError(provider string, resp *http.Response) error {
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	pe := &subtitles.ProviderError{Provider: provider, Err: fmt.Errorf("http %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))}

	if ra := resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"); ra != "" {
		if secs, err := strconv.Atoi(ra); err == nil {
			pe.RetryAfter = time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
		}
	}

	switch resp.StatusCode {
	case http.StatusBadRequest:
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindConfig
	case http.StatusUnauthorized, http.StatusForbidden:
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindAuth
	case http.StatusNotAcceptable: // 406
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindDownloadLimitExceeded
	case http.StatusTooManyRequests: // 429
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindTooManyRequests
	case http.StatusBadGateway: // 502
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindAPIThrottled
	case http.StatusGone: // 410, download link expired
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindParse
	default:
		pe.Kind = subtitles.KindServiceUnavailable
	}
	return pe
}
```

```go
package gestdown

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"

	common "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/tracing"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

const defaultEndpoint = "https://api.gestdown.info"

type Config struct {
	Endpoint   string
	HTTPClient *http.Client
}

type Provider struct{ cfg Config }

func New(cfg Config) *Provider {
	if cfg.Endpoint == "" {
		cfg.Endpoint = defaultEndpoint
	}
	if cfg.HTTPClient == nil {
		cfg.HTTPClient = http.DefaultClient
	}
	return &Provider{cfg: cfg}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string       { return "gestdown" }
func (p *Provider) HIVerifiable() bool { return false } // not in note §4.1's hearing_impaired_verifiable list
func (p *Provider) Capabilities() subtitles.Capabilities {
	return subtitles.Capabilities{Episodes: true} // TV only, research note §4.2
}

type searchResponse struct {
	MatchingSubtitles []struct {
		ID               string `json:"id"`
		Version          string `json:"version"`
		DownloadURI      string `json:"downloadUri"`
		HearingImpaired  bool   `json:"hearingImpaired"`
	} `json:"matchingSubtitles"`
}

func (p *Provider) Search(ctx context.Context, q subtitles.Query) ([]subtitles.Candidate, error) {
	if q.Kind != common.MediaKindEpisode {
		return nil, nil // TV only
	}
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.gestdown.search")
	defer span.End()

	lang := "en"
	if len(q.Languages) > 0 {
		if l, _, _, err := subtitles.ParseLangKey(q.Languages[0]); err == nil {
			lang = l
		}
	}
	url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/subtitles/get/%s/%d/%d/%s", p.cfg.Endpoint, q.IDs["tvdb"], q.Season, q.Episode, lang)

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	resp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: gestdown search: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusLocked { // 423 "refreshing, retry in 30s" — research note §4.2
		err := &subtitles.ProviderError{Provider: p.Name(), Kind: subtitles.KindServiceUnavailable, RetryAfter: 30 * timeSecond}
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, err
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		err := &subtitles.ProviderError{Provider: p.Name(), Kind: subtitles.KindServiceUnavailable, Err: fmt.Errorf("http %d", resp.StatusCode)}
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, err
	}

	var sr searchResponse
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&sr); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: gestdown search: decode: %w", err)
	}
	out := make([]subtitles.Candidate, 0, len(sr.MatchingSubtitles))
	for _, m := range sr.MatchingSubtitles {
		out = append(out, subtitles.Candidate{
			Provider: p.Name(), ID: m.ID, FetchID: m.ID, Language: lang,
			HI: m.HearingImpaired, ReleaseInfo: m.Version,
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (p *Provider) Download(ctx context.Context, c subtitles.Candidate) ([]byte, string, error) {
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.gestdown.download")
	defer span.End()

	// The search response's downloadUri is relative; Download is given only
	// the Candidate, so it re-derives the fixed path shape from FetchID
	// (Gestdown's IDs are opaque tokens the download endpoint accepts
	// directly — confirm this against the same gestdown.py source as
	// Step 41 before shipping).
	url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/subtitles/download/%s", p.cfg.Endpoint, c.FetchID)
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	resp, err := p.cfg.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: gestdown download: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		err := &subtitles.ProviderError{Provider: p.Name(), Kind: subtitles.KindServiceUnavailable, Err: fmt.Errorf("http %d", resp.StatusCode)}
		tracing.RecordError(span, err)
		return nil, "", err
	}
	raw, err := ioReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	return raw, c.ReleaseInfo + ".srt", nil
}
```

- [ ] **Step 45: Implement `provider.go`'s `Search` (embedded)**

```go
package embedded

import (
	"context"
	"strconv"

	common "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

// textCodecs are the codecs ffmpeg can losslessly extract as text
// subtitles (research note §3.1, §4.6): subrip, ass, ssa, webvtt, mov_text.
var textCodecs = map[string]bool{"subrip": true, "ass": true, "ssa": true, "webvtt": true, "mov_text": true}

type Config struct {
	FFmpeg string
	Path   string
	Info   common.MediaInfo
	IgnorePGS, IgnoreVobSub, IgnoreASS, SkipCommentary bool
}

type Provider struct{ cfg Config }

func New(cfg Config) *Provider {
	if cfg.FFmpeg == "" {
		cfg.FFmpeg = "ffmpeg"
	}
	return &Provider{cfg: cfg}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string       { return "embedded" }
func (p *Provider) HIVerifiable() bool { return true }
func (p *Provider) Capabilities() subtitles.Capabilities {
	return subtitles.Capabilities{Movies: true, Episodes: true, ForcedSearch: true, HashVerifiable: true}
}

func (p *Provider) Search(ctx context.Context, q subtitles.Query) ([]subtitles.Candidate, error) {
	var out []subtitles.Candidate
	for _, s := range p.cfg.Info.Subtitles {
		if s.Bitmap || !textCodecs[s.Codec] {
			continue
		}
		if p.cfg.IgnoreASS && (s.Codec == "ass" || s.Codec == "ssa") {
			continue
		}
		if p.cfg.SkipCommentary && containsFold(s.Title, "commentary") {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, subtitles.Candidate{
			Provider: p.Name(), FetchID: strconv.Itoa(int(s.Index)),
			Language: s.Language, HI: s.HearingImpaired, Forced: s.Forced,
			Matches: map[string]bool{subtitles.MatchHash: true, subtitles.MatchHearingImpaired: true},
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func containsFold(haystack, needle string) bool {
	return len(needle) > 0 && len(haystack) >= len(needle) && stringsContainsFold(haystack, needle)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 47: Implement `Download` (embedded, ffmpeg exec)**

Append to `provider.go`:
```go
import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os/exec"
	"strconv"

	common "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/tracing"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

func (p *Provider) Download(ctx context.Context, c subtitles.Candidate) ([]byte, string, error) {
	ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "subtitles.embedded.download")
	defer span.End()

	if _, err := strconv.Atoi(c.FetchID); err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("subtitles: embedded: invalid stream index %q: %w", c.FetchID, err)
	}

	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, p.cfg.FFmpeg, "-y", "-i", p.cfg.Path, "-map", "0:"+c.FetchID, "-c:s", "srt", "-f", "srt", "pipe:1")
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		wrapped := fmt.Errorf("subtitles: embedded ffmpeg extract (stream %s): %w: %s", c.FetchID, err, stderr.String())
		tracing.RecordError(span, wrapped)
		return nil, "", wrapped
	}
	return stdout.Bytes(), "stream-" + c.FetchID + ".srt", nil
}
```
(Merge this import block with the one Step 45 already added — do not duplicate `common`/`subtitles` imports.)
